operations.specification: Create a new guest account using device fingerprint identification. The service generates a unique guest ID and stores the device_fingerprint for future recognition. A new guest session is created with access and refresh tokens, connection metadata (IP, href, referrer), and expiration timestamp. The device_fingerprint must be unique - if a guest with the same fingerprint exists, return the existing guest's tokens instead of creating a duplicate. Tokens are JWT-based with appropriate expiration times for temporary guest access.
operations.description:
Register a new guest account or recognize returning guest by device fingerprint.

This endpoint creates a new guest account in the hrm_platform_guests table when a device fingerprint is encountered for the first time. The device_fingerprint field serves as the unique identifier for guest recognition across sessions, enabling continuity without requiring email/password authentication.

For returning guests with an existing device_fingerprint, the operation recognizes the guest and issues new session tokens without creating a duplicate account. This supports the temporary, frictionless access model for unauthenticated platform visitors.

Upon successful guest registration or recognition, a new session record is created in hrm_platform_guest_sessions with access_token, refresh_token, and connection metadata (ip, href, referrer). The session includes an expired_at timestamp for automatic invalidation.

The response contains the guest's authorized tokens (access and refresh) along with guest identification, enabling immediate platform access for temporary visitors.

requestBody.description: Device fingerprint for guest identification and recognition.

responseBody.description: Guest authentication tokens and identification for temporary platform access.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Refresh guest session tokens using the provided refresh token. The service validates the refresh token against hrm_platform_guest_sessions, checks expiration, and generates new access and refresh tokens. The existing session is updated with new tokens and extended expiration. Invalid or expired refresh tokens result in authentication failure, requiring the guest to re-join via the join endpoint.
operations.description:
Refresh guest session tokens to extend platform access.

This endpoint enables guests to renew their authentication tokens without re-submitting their device fingerprint. The operation validates the provided refresh_token against the hrm_platform_guest_sessions table, ensuring the session exists and has not expired based on the expired_at timestamp.

Upon successful validation, new JWT access and refresh tokens are generated and the session record is updated with the new tokens and extended expiration time. This maintains the guest's temporary access continuity while enforcing security through token rotation.

If the refresh token is invalid, expired, or not found, the operation fails and the guest must re-authenticate through the join endpoint. This ensures that expired or compromised sessions cannot be renewed.

The response returns fresh tokens (access and refresh) along with updated session expiration information, allowing the guest client to maintain seamless platform access.

requestBody.description: Refresh token for session renewal.

responseBody.description: New guest authentication tokens and updated session information.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: Validate email format and uniqueness against hrm_platform_members.email unique constraint. Hash password using bcrypt with appropriate salt rounds. Create member record with provided email, password_hash, display_name, avatar_url, and phone_number. Set created_at and updated_at timestamps. Generate JWT access token and refresh token. Create session record in hrm_platform_member_sessions with tokens, IP, href, referrer, and expired_at. Return IHrmPlatformMember.IAuthorized with tokens and member details.
operations.description:
Creates a new member account with email and password authentication credentials.

This endpoint enables new users to register for the HRM platform by providing their email address, password, and initial profile information. The email address serves as the unique identifier for authentication and must not already exist in the hrm_platform_members table. The password is securely hashed using bcrypt before storage, ensuring credentials are never stored in plain text.

Upon successful registration, the system automatically creates an authentication session and returns JWT tokens (access_token and refresh_token) in the IHrmPlatformMember.IAuthorized response. The access token enables immediate API authentication, while the refresh token allows token renewal without re-authentication. Session metadata including IP address, current page URL (href), and referrer URL are captured for audit trail purposes.

The display_name field becomes the user's global profile identifier shown across all organizations they may join. Optional avatar_url and phone_number fields can be provided during registration or updated later through profile management endpoints. The created_at timestamp marks the account creation time, and the account is immediately active for use.

This operation integrates with the hrm_platform_members table structure, utilizing the unique email constraint to prevent duplicate accounts. New members can subsequently create or join organizations and perform HRM operations based on their assigned role permissions.

requestBody.description: Registration information for creating a new member account

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and member information for newly registered account

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Look up member by email in hrm_platform_members table. Verify account is not soft-deleted (deleted_at is null). Compare provided password with password_hash using bcrypt. Generate JWT access token and refresh token. Create new session in hrm_platform_member_sessions with tokens, client IP, href, referrer, and expired_at timestamp. Return IHrmPlatformMember.IAuthorized with tokens and member profile information.
operations.description:
Authenticates existing member credentials and establishes a new JWT session.

This endpoint validates member authentication credentials by verifying the provided email and password combination against the hrm_platform_members table. The email address is looked up in the unique email index, and the provided password is hashed and compared against the stored password_hash using bcrypt comparison. Successful authentication confirms the member's identity and grants platform access.

Upon successful credential validation, the system creates a new session record in hrm_platform_member_sessions with freshly generated JWT tokens. The access_token enables authenticated API requests, while the refresh_token allows seamless token renewal without requiring re-authentication. Session metadata is captured including the client's IP address, current page URL (href), and referrer URL for security audit and anomaly detection purposes.

The expired_at timestamp in the session record enforces session lifetime limits for security compliance. Multiple concurrent sessions are supported, allowing members to maintain active sessions across different devices or browsers. Each login creates a distinct session record with unique tokens.

Failed authentication attempts (invalid email or password mismatch) return appropriate error responses without revealing whether the email exists or the password was incorrect, preventing user enumeration attacks. Members with deleted_at set (soft-deleted accounts) cannot authenticate and receive access denied responses.

requestBody.description: Login credentials for member authentication

responseBody.description: Authentication tokens and member information for successful login

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Validate refresh_token exists in hrm_platform_member_sessions.refresh_token unique index. Verify session expired_at is in the future. Retrieve associated member from hrm_platform_members via member_id relation. Generate new JWT access token and refresh token pair. Update session record with new tokens and extended expired_at timestamp. Optionally update IP, href, referrer if provided. Return IHrmPlatformMember.IAuthorized with new tokens and current member profile.
operations.description:
Renews authentication tokens using a valid refresh token without requiring re-authentication.

This endpoint enables members to obtain new JWT tokens when their access token expires, maintaining continuous platform access without requiring credential re-entry. The refresh_token from the request body is validated against the hrm_platform_member_sessions table's unique refresh_token index to verify session validity and authenticity.

The system verifies the session has not expired by checking the expired_at timestamp against the current time. Expired sessions are rejected, requiring the member to log in again with credentials. Valid refresh tokens result in the generation of a new access_token and refresh_token pair, implementing token rotation for enhanced security.

The existing session record in hrm_platform_member_sessions is updated with the new tokens and refreshed expired_at timestamp, extending the session lifetime. Connection metadata (IP, href, referrer) can be optionally updated if the refresh request originates from a different context, providing accurate audit trail information.

This token refresh mechanism supports seamless user experience while maintaining security through token expiration and rotation. Members can maintain long-lived sessions through periodic refresh operations, while compromised tokens can be invalidated by session deletion. The IHrmPlatformMember.IAuthorized response provides the new token pair for continued authenticated API access.

requestBody.description: Refresh token for obtaining new authentication tokens

responseBody.description: New authentication tokens and member information

Access is restricted to organization members with appropriate administrative permissions. Guest accounts represent temporary platform access and can be converted to member accounts through the registration process.

The guest record provides visibility into pre-authentication visitor state and is used for tracking guest sessions and device identification. This endpoint is typically used during the authentication flow to verify guest status before transitioning to member actor.

No authorization is required as guest data is not organization-scoped and represents anonymous visitor state.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of authenticated member's session records with filtering capabilities.

This operation provides members with visibility into their active and historical login sessions. Each session record includes connection metadata such as IP address, page URL, and referrer along with token expiration information.

Sessions can be filtered by creation date range and expiration status to identify currently active sessions or review historical login activity. The response includes session summaries optimized for list displays with essential authentication and connection information.

This endpoint is useful for security auditing, allowing users to monitor their account access and identify any unauthorized sessions. Active sessions can be distinguished by comparing expired_at with the current timestamp.

Return session summaries including ip, href, referrer, created_at, expired_at fields. Exclude access_token and refresh_token from response for security. Sort results by created_at descending by default to show most recent sessions first.

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific member authentication session.

This operation returns comprehensive session details including the JWT access and refresh tokens, connection metadata (IP address, current page URL, referrer), and temporal information (creation and expiration timestamps). The session represents an authenticated login instance for a member account.

Session data is used for authentication management, allowing users to view their active sessions and understand session lifecycle. The expired_at field indicates when the session will no longer be valid for API authentication.

This endpoint is typically used in session management interfaces where users can review their login history and active sessions. Combined with session listing operations, users can identify and manage their authentication state across different devices and locations.

Access is restricted to the session owner (the member whose member_id matches the session record) to ensure privacy and security of authentication credentials.

operations.description:
Update the authenticated member's global profile information.

This operation allows members to modify their profile attributes including display name, avatar image URL, and phone number. These profile changes are global and apply across all organizations the member belongs to, ensuring consistent identity presentation throughout the platform.

Members can update any combination of profile fields in a single request. Unspecified fields retain their current values. The display name is required for identification in the UI and must be provided during initial registration. Avatar URL and phone number are optional fields that can be set or cleared.

This endpoint enforces that members can only update their own profile. The member identity is derived from the authenticated session context, preventing unauthorized modifications to other users' profiles. Email address and password cannot be changed through this endpoint - those require dedicated account management operations.

Upon successful update, the operation returns the complete updated member object with the new profile values and updated timestamp. The updated_at field reflects when the profile was last modified.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Update the authenticated member's profile by extracting member ID from session context.

Validate request body fields:
- display_name: optional string, trim whitespace, validate length (1-100 characters)
- avatar_url: optional string or null, validate URL format if provided
- phone_number: optional string or null, validate phone format if provided

Apply partial update: only update fields that are explicitly provided in the request body. Unspecified fields retain their current values.

Set updated_at timestamp to current time.

Return the complete updated IHrmPlatformMember object including all profile fields.

Authorization: member actor only, scoped to own profile (enforced by session context).

Retrieve a specific member account by their unique identifier.

This operation returns the complete member profile information including authentication credentials (email), display name, avatar image URL, and contact phone number. The member profile is global and shared across all organizations the member belongs to.

Access to member information is restricted based on organization context and user permissions. Members can typically access their own profile information, and users with appropriate administrative permissions can view other members' profiles within their organization.

The response includes all member attributes except the password hash, which is never exposed through the API for security reasons. Profile information such as display name and avatar are consistent regardless of which organization context the member is currently working in.

This endpoint is commonly used when displaying user profile pages, editing profile settings, or verifying member identity in organizational contexts.

operations.description:
Update the authenticated member's global profile information including display name, avatar image URL, and phone number.

This operation allows members to modify their personal profile attributes that are shared across all organizations they belong to. The display name serves as the primary identifier shown throughout the interface and in activity logs. The avatar URL provides visual personalization, and the phone number enables contact capabilities. All profile changes are applied immediately and reflected across all organization contexts.

The member's identity is derived from the authenticated session context, ensuring users can only modify their own profile. The display_name field is required and must be provided in every update request. The avatar_url and phone_number fields are optional and can be set to null to remove existing values.

Upon successful update, the system propagates the display_name change to all associated employee records to maintain denormalized search efficiency. This ensures that employee searches and filters remain accurate without requiring joins to the members table.

Related operations include GET /profile for retrieving current profile information and POST /auth/login for authentication. Profile edits are restricted to the profile owner - attempts to access or modify another user's profile are rejected.
operations.name: update

Accept display_name (required), avatar_url (optional), and phone_number (optional) fields in the request body. Validate that display_name is provided and not empty. Update the member record with the new profile values and update the updated_at timestamp. After successful update, propagate the display_name change to all associated hrm_platform_employees records to maintain denormalized search efficiency. Return the updated member object. Ensure the operation only modifies the authenticated member's own profile - the member ID must come from session context, not from request parameters.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of organizations accessible to the authenticated user.

This operation provides search capabilities for organizations based on name partial matching, owner filtering, and creation date ranges. The results are strictly scoped to organizations where the user has membership, enforcing multi-tenancy data isolation policies.

Each organization in the response includes summary information such as name, description, logo URL, currency, timezone, and fiscal start month. Detailed organization information can be obtained by calling GET /organizations/{organizationId} with a specific organization identifier.

The operation supports comprehensive pagination with configurable page sizes and sorting options. Users belonging to multiple organizations will see all organizations they have access to, filtered by the provided search criteria.

Authentication is required as a member actor. Guest users cannot access this endpoint. The system enforces organization context validation on every request to prevent cross-organization data access.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query hrm_platform_organizations table with pagination and filtering support.

Apply search filters on name (partial match using LIKE), owner_id (exact match), and created_at date range. Filter results to only include organizations where the authenticated user has membership (either as owner or as employee).

Join with hrm_platform_employees to verify user's organizational membership. Exclude soft-deleted organizations (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) from results.

Support cursor-based or offset-based pagination with configurable page size (default 20, max 100). Allow sorting by name, created_at, or updated_at in ascending or descending order.

Return organization summary fields: id, name, description, logo_url, currency, timezone, fiscal_start_month, created_at. Do not include owner_id in response to avoid exposing internal references.

Handle edge cases: user with no organization membership returns empty array, search with no matching results returns empty data array with pagination metadata.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of organization summaries

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific organization by its unique identifier.

This endpoint provides complete organization configuration including ownership details, branding settings, and operational parameters. The response includes the organization's name, description, logo URL, currency code, timezone setting, and fiscal year start month. This information is essential for displaying organization context in the user interface and configuring organization-specific features.

Access is restricted to member actors who belong to the target organization. The system enforces strict data isolation, ensuring users can only access organizations they are members of. When a user belongs to multiple organizations, this endpoint retrieves information for the specific organization identified in the path parameter.

The organization owner information is included to support ownership verification and transfer workflows. Timestamps for creation, last update, and soft deletion are provided for audit and synchronization purposes. If the organization has been soft-deleted, access is denied unless the caller has administrative privileges.

This operation is commonly used during organization context switching, settings page displays, and when validating organization membership before performing organization-scoped actions.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query the hrm_platform_organizations table by the provided organizationId UUID parameter. Verify the requesting member belongs to the organization by checking membership through the hrm_platform_employees table where employee user_id matches the authenticated member's id and employee organization_id matches the requested organizationId. Return 403 Forbidden if membership verification fails. Include the owner relation to fetch owner member details. Exclude soft-deleted organizations (deleted_at is not null) from normal access. Return the complete organization entity with all fields: id, owner_id, name, description, logo_url, currency, timezone, fiscal_start_month, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at. Handle the case where organizationId does not exist by returning 404 Not Found.

responseBody.description: Complete organization information including settings and ownership details

operations.description:
Create a new organization workspace within the HRM platform.

This operation allows authenticated members to create a new organization, which serves as an independent multi-tenant workspace. The member who creates the organization becomes its owner with full administrative control. Organizations operate independently with strict data isolation - employees, projects, departments, roles, and all business data belong exclusively to that organization and are not visible to members of other organizations.

The organization owner can configure settings including name, description, logo image, currency code, timezone, and fiscal year start month. These settings govern financial calculations, timesheet week boundaries, and reporting periods for all operations within the organization.

Upon successful creation, the system automatically assigns the creator as the organization owner with the built-in Owner role. The owner gains access to all organization management features including employee management, role configuration, project oversight, and organization deletion. The organization is immediately available for use, and the member can switch to it via organization context management endpoints.

This endpoint enforces that the requesting user must be an authenticated member. Guest actors cannot create organizations. The owner_id field is automatically populated from the authenticated session and cannot be overridden in the request body.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new hrm_platform_organizations record with the following implementation steps:

1. Validate request body: name (required, non-empty), currency (required, valid ISO 4217 code), timezone (required, valid IANA identifier), fiscal_start_month (required, integer 1-12), description and logo_url (optional).

2. Extract owner_id from authenticated member session context. The owner must be an active member account.

3. Generate UUID for the new organization id.

4. Set created_at and updated_at to current timestamp. Set deleted_at to null.

5. Insert the organization record into hrm_platform_organizations table within a database transaction.

6. The member is automatically granted Owner role for this organization through the ownership relationship (owner_id foreign key).

7. Return the complete organization object including all fields.

8. Log the organization creation in hrm_platform_activity_logs with action type 'organization.created'.

Error handling:
- Return 400 if required fields are missing or invalid format
- Return 401 if user is not authenticated (guest actor)
- Return 500 for database transaction failures

responseBody.description: Created organization with full details

requestBody.description: Organization creation information

operations.description:
Update an existing organization's configuration settings.

This operation allows organization owners to modify their organization's profile and settings including the organization name, description, logo image URL, currency code, timezone, and fiscal year start month. All changes are validated against business rules and the updated organization entity is returned.

Only the organization owner has permission to update organization settings. The system enforces strict ownership validation on every request to ensure data isolation between organizations. Members who are not owners cannot access this endpoint.

The organization's owner_id cannot be modified through this endpoint. To transfer ownership, a separate ownership transfer operation must be used. System-managed fields including created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at are automatically handled by the system and cannot be modified directly.

This operation is essential for organization administrators to configure their workspace settings, branding, and financial reporting parameters. Changes take effect immediately and are reflected across all organization-scoped operations.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Query hrm_platform_organizations table by organizationId UUID.
Validate that the requesting member is the organization owner by comparing member.id with organization.owner_id.
If member is not owner, throw 403 Forbidden error.
Validate all provided fields against business rules:
- name: required, non-empty string
- description: optional string
- logo_url: optional string, valid URL format
- currency: required, valid ISO 4217 currency code (USD, EUR, KRW, etc.)
- timezone: required, valid IANA timezone identifier
- fiscal_start_month: required, integer 1-12
Apply partial update - only update fields provided in request body.
Set updated_at timestamp to current time.
Save changes to database within transaction.
Log activity if audit logging is enabled.
Return updated organization entity with all fields.
Handle concurrent update conflicts with optimistic locking if version field exists.

requestBody.description: Organization configuration fields to update

operations.description:
Permanently delete an organization and all associated business data.

This operation allows organization owners to delete their organization. Before deletion, the system validates that all pending timesheets are resolved (approved or rejected) and there are no active employee contracts. If these conditions are not met, the deletion request is rejected.

When an organization is deleted, all employees, departments, projects, tasks, timelogs, timesheets, roles, contracts, and activity logs associated with that organization are permanently removed from the system. This deletion is irreversible and cannot be undone. The owner's member account remains intact but is no longer associated with any organization.

Only the organization owner (the member whose ID matches the owner_id field) can delete the organization. Members with other roles cannot delete the organization regardless of their permissions.

After successful deletion, the owner must either create a new organization or join another existing organization to continue using the platform.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Delete an organization by marking deleted_at timestamp.

Validation logic:
1. Verify requester is the organization owner (member.id === organization.owner_id)
2. Query all timesheets for this organization where status is 'draft' or 'submitted' - if any exist, reject with 400 error
3. Query all employee contracts where end_date is null or in the future - if any active contracts exist, reject with 400 error
4. If validation passes, set deleted_at to current timestamp in a transaction

Cascade deletion (handled by database foreign key constraints with onDelete: Cascade):
- All hrm_platform_employees records
- All hrm_platform_departments records
- All hrm_platform_projects records (and related project_members, tasks, task_histories)
- All hrm_platform_roles records (and related role_permissions)
- All hrm_platform_employee_contracts records
- All hrm_platform_timelogs records
- All hrm_platform_timesheets records
- All hrm_platform_timers records
- All hrm_platform_activity_logs records for this organization

Return 204 No Content on success. Return 400 Bad Request with validation error details if timesheets or contracts block deletion. Return 403 Forbidden if requester is not the owner. Return 404 Not Found if organization doesn't exist or is already deleted.

prerequisites.description: Organization must be created before it can be deleted. This prerequisite ensures the organization resource exists with a valid owner_id reference.

operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated and filtered list of employee records within the current organization context.

This operation provides comprehensive search capabilities for browsing employees across the organization. Users can filter results by department assignment, employment type classification, and employment status. The display name field supports partial text matching using trigram-based search for efficient name lookups.

All results are strictly scoped to the currently selected organization, enforcing data isolation policies. Employees from other organizations are never visible, even if the authenticated user belongs to multiple organizations.

The endpoint supports cursor-based pagination with configurable page sizes and multiple sorting options including display name, employment type, status, and creation date. Response includes employee summary information optimized for list displays, showing essential fields like display name, position, employment type, status, and department reference.

Users with employee:view permission can access this endpoint to browse the employee directory. Users with employee:manage permission additionally see all employees including deactivated records for administrative purposes.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query hrm_platform_employees table with organization context filtering. Apply WHERE clause for organization_id matching current session context. Support filtering by department_id (exact match), employment_type (enum match), status (enum match), and display_name (trigram search using gin_trgm_ops index). Implement cursor-based pagination with limit and cursor parameters. Support sorting by display_name, employment_type, status, created_at with ascending/descending order. Join with hrm_platform_departments for department name if needed. Exclude soft-deleted records (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) unless requester has employee:manage permission. Return IPageIHrmPlatformEmployee.ISummary with pagination metadata and employee summary array.

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information for a specific employee record within the organization.

This operation returns comprehensive employee data including the employee's linkage to their user account, organization context, assigned role, optional department assignment, position title, employment classification, and current status. The display_name field is denormalized from the member's global profile to enable efficient search and filtering without requiring joins.

Access to this endpoint requires the member actor to have employee:view or employee:manage permission within the current organization context. The employee record must belong to the organization associated with the user's current session to ensure data isolation.

The response includes all employee attributes: member_id referencing the user account, organization_id for organizational context, role_id for permission assignment, optional department_id for organizational structure, position as job title, employment_type categorizing the worker relationship (full-time, part-time, contractor, intern), and status indicating whether the employee is active or deactivated. Deactivated employees cannot log time or submit timesheets but their historical data like timelogs and timesheets is preserved.

Timestamps include created_at for record creation, updated_at for last modification, and deleted_at for soft deletion tracking. A null deleted_at indicates an active employee, while a populated value indicates deactivation timestamp.

This operation is typically used after retrieving the employee list via PATCH /employees to view detailed information for a specific employee. Related operations include PATCH /employees for list retrieval with filtering, PUT /employees/{employeeId} for updating employee details, and PATCH /employees for searching employees by name or filtering by department, employment type, or status.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the hrm_platform_employees table by the provided employeeId UUID parameter.

Validate that the employee record exists and belongs to the user's current organization context. If the employee's organization_id does not match the session's organization, return 404 to maintain data isolation.

Check user permissions: require employee:view or employee:manage permission. Users without these permissions receive 403 Forbidden.

Include related entity references in the response: member, organization, role, and department (if assigned). The department relation is optional and may be null.

Return the complete employee record with all fields: id, member_id, organization_id, role_id, department_id, display_name, position, employment_type, status, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at.

Handle soft deletion: deleted_at field indicates deactivation status. Both active and deactivated employees can be retrieved via this endpoint; the status field and deleted_at timestamp indicate the current state.

Error handling: Return 404 if employee not found or belongs to different organization. Return 403 if user lacks required permissions. Return 401 if user is not authenticated.

responseBody.description: Detailed employee information including role, department, position, and employment details

operations.description:
Create a new employee record representing organizational membership within the current organization context.

This operation establishes a linkage between a user account (member) and the organization, creating an employee record that enables the user to operate within the organization's context. The employee record includes role assignment determining permissions, optional department assignment for organizational structure, position title, employment classification, and initial employment status.

The display_name field is denormalized from the member's global profile to enable efficient employee search and filtering without requiring joins. Employment type categorizes the worker relationship as full-time, part-time, contractor, or intern. Status indicates whether the employee is currently active or deactivated.

This operation requires the employee:manage permission. The creating user must specify a valid role_id belonging to the organization, and optionally a department_id if the employee should be assigned to a specific department. The member_id must reference an existing user account. If the email corresponds to a pending invitation, the system should link the invitation to the created employee record.

The operation enforces a unique constraint on (member_id, organization_id), ensuring each user can have only one employee record per organization. Attempting to create a duplicate employee record for the same user in the same organization will be rejected.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new employee record in the hrm_platform_employees table with the following implementation steps:

1. Validate the requesting user has employee:manage permission within the current organization context
2. Verify the member_id references an existing user in hrm_platform_members table
3. Verify the role_id references a valid role belonging to the current organization
4. If department_id is provided, verify it references a valid department in the current organization
5. Check unique constraint: query hrm_platform_employees for existing record with same (member_id, organization_id) - reject if found
6. Denormalize display_name from member's global profile if not explicitly provided
7. Set initial status to 'active' if not specified
8. Insert new employee record with generated UUID for id, current timestamp for created_at and updated_at
9. Log the employee creation action to hrm_platform_activity_logs with action type 'employee_invited' or 'employee_created'
10. Return the complete employee record including all fields and relationship IDs

Edge cases to handle:
- Reject if member already has an employee record in this organization (unique constraint violation)
- Reject if role does not belong to the current organization (data isolation)
- Reject if department does not belong to the current organization (data isolation)
- Handle concurrent creation attempts with database-level unique constraint enforcement

responseBody.description: Created employee record with complete information including generated ID and timestamps

requestBody.description: Employee creation information including member reference, role assignment, and employment details

operations.description:
Update an existing employee record's organizational membership details including role assignment, department affiliation, position, employment type, and status.

This operation allows users with employee:manage permission to modify employee records within their organization. Updates can include changing the employee's assigned role (which immediately affects their permissions), reassigning to a different department for organizational restructuring, updating job title/position, changing employment classification (full-time, part-time, contractor, intern), or activating/deactivating the employee.

The employee record represents the linkage between a user account and an organization, establishing their membership and access context. When an employee is deactivated (status changed to deactivated), they cannot log time or submit timesheets, but historical data like timelogs and timesheets are preserved. The display_name field is denormalized from the member's global profile for search efficiency.

Department assignment is optional - when set to null, the employee remains active but is not categorized under any department. Role assignment is required and must reference a valid role within the same organization. Built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) always exist and can be assigned. Custom roles can only be assigned if they belong to the organization.

The operation enforces organization context isolation - employees can only be updated within the caller's current organization context. The unique constraint on (member_id, organization_id) ensures each user has only one employee record per organization.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Update employee record by employeeId UUID.

1. Validate employee:manage permission for current user in organization context
2. Query hrm_platform_employees by employeeId with organization context filter
3. Validate employee exists and belongs to caller's organization
4. Validate role_id references a valid role in the same organization (if provided)
5. Validate department_id references a valid department in the same organization or is null (if provided)
6. Validate employment_type is one of: full-time, part-time, contractor, intern (if provided)
7. Validate status is one of: active, deactivated (if provided)
8. Update employee record with provided fields
9. Update updated_at timestamp to current time
10. If status changed to deactivated, set deleted_at timestamp; if reactivated, clear deleted_at
11. Return updated employee record with all fields

Edge cases:
- Employee not found: 404 error
- Role/department not in organization: 400 error
- Insufficient permission: 403 error
- Organization context mismatch: 400 error

responseBody.description: Updated employee record with all fields

requestBody.description: Employee update fields: role assignment, department affiliation, position, employment type, and status

prerequisites.description: Employee record must be created before it can be updated. The employeeId path parameter references an existing employee that was created through the employee creation endpoint.

operations.description:
Deactivate an employee record by setting the deleted_at timestamp and changing status to deactivated, effectively removing the employee from active organizational membership while preserving all historical data.

This operation performs a soft delete on the employee record, marking it as deactivated without permanently removing it from the database. The employee's status is changed to deactivated, preventing them from logging time entries, submitting timesheets, or accessing organization resources. However, all historical records including timelogs, timesheets, task assignments, and project memberships are preserved for audit and reporting purposes.

Only users with the employee:manage permission within the organization can deactivate employees. The system validates that the requesting user has appropriate permissions and that the employee belongs to the same organization context. An employee cannot be deactivated if they are the only active employee with organization management permissions - at least one active employee with organization management permissions must remain.

Once deactivated, the employee record can be reactivated through the update endpoint by clearing the deleted_at timestamp and setting status back to active. Historical records that reference the deactivated employee maintain their integrity and continue to appear in reports and audits with the employee's display name preserved at the time of deactivation.

This operation is distinct from user account deletion - it only removes the employee's membership from a specific organization, not their global user account. The user may still have employee records in other organizations.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification: Query the hrm_platform_employees table to verify the employee exists and belongs to the requesting user's organization context. Validate that the authenticated user has employee:manage permission within the organization. Check that the employee is not the sole owner of the organization - if the employee has the Owner role, verify there are other active employees with Owner role before allowing deactivation. Begin a database transaction. Update the employee record by setting deleted_at to the current timestamp and status to 'deactivated'. This soft delete approach preserves all foreign key relationships and historical data. Commit the transaction. Create an activity log entry recording the employee deactivation action with timestamp, user who performed it, and target employee ID. Return 204 No Content on success. If the employee has an active timer, automatically stop the timer and create a timelog entry before deactivation. If the employee has draft timesheets, they remain in draft state but cannot be submitted while deactivated.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of organizational departments.

This operation provides advanced search capabilities for browsing departments within the current organization context. Users can filter departments by name, parent department, and hierarchy level. The endpoint supports comprehensive pagination with configurable page sizes and sorting options.

All employees in the organization can access this endpoint to view the department structure. The response includes department summary information optimized for list displays, showing names, descriptions, and hierarchical relationships.

Results are scoped to the authenticated user's organization through session context. Departments are returned with their parent department references to enable client-side hierarchy reconstruction. The one-level nesting constraint ensures simple organizational structures.
operations.name: index
operations.specification: Query hrm_platform_departments table with pagination and filtering. Apply search filters on name (partial match), parent_id (exact match for child departments), and hierarchy level (top-level vs sub-departments). Filter by hrm_platform_organization_id from session context. Join with hrm_platform_employees to include employee count per department if requested. Apply soft delete filter (deleted_at IS NULL) to exclude deleted departments. Support sorting by name, created_at. Return cursor-based pagination with IPageIHrmPlatformDepartment.ISummary response type. Validate organization context from member session.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of department summaries

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for department listing

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific department within the organization.

This operation returns complete department details including the department name, optional description, parent department reference for hierarchical structure, and audit timestamps. The department entity represents an organizational unit used for grouping employees within the organization structure.

All employees in the organization can access this endpoint to view department information. The response includes the full department record with all fields from the hrm_platform_departments table, enabling clients to display department details and understand the organizational hierarchy.

The department hierarchy supports one level of nesting, meaning a department can have a parent department but cannot have nested sub-departments beyond that single level. The parent_id field in the response indicates the department's position in the hierarchy, with null values representing top-level departments.

This endpoint is commonly used together with the department list endpoint (PATCH /departments) which provides summarized department information for browsing, while this endpoint provides complete details for a specific department.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the hrm_platform_departments table by the provided departmentId UUID parameter.

Retrieve the complete department record including: id, hrm_platform_organization_id, parent_id, name, description, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at.

Validate that the department exists and belongs to the authenticated user's organization context. Return 404 if department not found or belongs to different organization.

Include the parent department relationship if parent_id is not null. The organization context should be derived from the authenticated session, not from the request parameters.

Filter out soft-deleted departments (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) unless explicitly requesting deleted records.

responseBody.description: Complete department information with all fields and relationships

prerequisites.description: Department must be created before it can be retrieved by ID

operations.description:
Create a new organizational department within the current organization context.

This endpoint allows users with organization management permission (org:manage) to create new departments for grouping employees. The department requires a name that must be unique within the organization, and may include an optional description explaining the department's purpose. An optional parent department can be specified to establish a one-level hierarchical structure.

The system enforces the one-level hierarchy constraint: if a parent department is specified, that parent must be a top-level department (cannot have its own parent). This ensures departments cannot be nested beyond a single level. The department name is validated for uniqueness within the organization using the unique constraint on (hrm_platform_organization_id, name).

Upon successful creation, the department is assigned a UUID identifier and timestamps. The complete department entity is returned, including all fields. This operation is typically followed by assigning employees to the newly created department using the employee update endpoint.

Authorization requires the member actor role with org:manage permission. Users without this permission will receive an authorization error. The organization context is automatically derived from the authenticated user's session.
operations.name: create
operations.specification: Create a new department within the authenticated user's organization context. Query the hrm_platform_departments table to validate name uniqueness within the organization (hrm_platform_organization_id, name unique constraint). If parent_id is provided, verify the parent department exists and does not have its own parent (one-level hierarchy constraint - parent.parent_id must be null). Create the department record with hrm_platform_organization_id derived from the authenticated session, name, optional description, and optional parent_id. Set created_at and updated_at timestamps automatically. Return the complete department entity including the generated UUID. Log the action to hrm_platform_activity_logs if activity logging is enabled. Throw validation errors for duplicate names within organization or invalid parent hierarchy.

responseBody.description: Complete department entity with all fields including generated ID and timestamps

requestBody.description: Department creation information including name, optional description, and optional parent department reference

operations.description:
Update an existing department's details within the organization.

This operation allows users with organization management permission to modify department information including the department name, description, and parent department assignment. The department name must remain unique within the organization, and any parent department changes must respect the one-level hierarchy constraint.

The update operation validates that the department exists and is not soft deleted, the new name doesn't conflict with existing departments in the same organization, and if a parent department is specified, it belongs to the same organization and doesn't create multi-level nesting. The department being updated cannot be set as its own parent.

Related operations include GET /departments/{departmentId} for retrieving department details before editing, and PATCH /departments for listing all departments to select a valid parent department during the update process.
operations.name: update
operations.specification:
Query the hrm_platform_departments table by departmentId UUID, ensuring the record is not soft deleted (deleted_at is null). Validate the requesting user has org:manage permission in the current organization context.

For the update payload:
- Validate name is provided and non-empty
- Check name uniqueness within the organization (query hrm_platform_departments where hrm_platform_organization_id matches and name equals the new value, excluding the current department)
- If parent_id is provided, validate it exists in the same organization and is not the department itself
- Validate one-level hierarchy: the new parent must not have a parent itself (query parent's parent_id is null)

Perform the update transaction:
- Update name, description, and parent_id fields
- Set updated_at to current timestamp
- Return the updated department record

Handle edge cases:
- Department not found: return 404
- Name conflict: return 409 conflict error
- Invalid parent (creates multi-level hierarchy): return 400 bad request
- Insufficient permissions: return 403 forbidden
- Department is soft deleted: return 404

responseBody.description: Updated department information

requestBody.description: Department update fields

operations.description:
Remove a department from the organization by marking it as deleted.

This operation is restricted to users with organization management permissions (org:manage). When a department is deleted, all employees currently assigned to that department have their department reference set to null, preserving employee records while removing the organizational grouping. The deletion process validates that the department has no child departments, as the system maintains a one-level hierarchy structure.

The department is soft deleted by setting the deleted_at timestamp, which removes it from active queries while preserving historical records. Activity logs and employee department history records that reference the deleted department maintain their integrity for audit and compliance purposes. Per business rules, this deletion cannot be undone once completed.

Before deletion, the system validates that no child departments exist under the target department. If child departments are present, the deletion request is rejected with an appropriate error message indicating that child departments must be deleted or reassigned first. Related API operations include GET /departments for listing departments and PUT /departments/{departmentId} for updating department information.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Implement department soft deletion with the following logic:

1. Verify the authenticated user has org:manage permission for the target organization
2. Retrieve the department by ID and validate it belongs to the user's organization context
3. Check if the department has any child departments (children relation is not empty)
4. If child departments exist, reject the request with 400 Bad Request indicating child departments must be handled first
5. Begin database transaction
6. Update all employees with hrm_platform_department_id pointing to this department, setting their department reference to null
7. Set the department's deleted_at timestamp to current time
8. Create an activity log entry recording the department deletion action
9. Commit transaction
10. Return 204 No Content on success

Edge cases to handle:
- Department not found: return 404 Not Found
- User lacks org:manage permission: return 403 Forbidden
- Department already deleted: return 404 Not Found (treat as non-existent)
- Department has child departments: return 400 Bad Request with descriptive error

prerequisites.description: Department must be created before it can be deleted

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of employee department assignment history records.

This operation provides audit trail access for tracking when employees were assigned to or removed from departments. Each history entry captures the employee, the department assignment (null when removed), the member who made the change, and the timestamp of the change.

Supports comprehensive filtering by employee, department, change author, and date ranges. Results are paginated with configurable page sizes and sorting options. This endpoint is intended for organizational audit and compliance purposes, allowing users with organization management permissions to review department structure changes over time.

The history records are immutable and append-only, providing a complete audit trail of all department assignment changes. When a department is deleted, the department_id in history records remains preserved for historical accuracy.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query hrm_platform_employee_department_histories table with pagination and filtering.

Apply search filters on:
- employee_id: Filter by specific employee UUID
- department_id: Filter by specific department UUID (include null for removed assignments)
- changed_by_id: Filter by member who made the change
- changed_at: Filter by date range (from/to)
- created_at: Filter by record creation date range

Join with hrm_platform_employees for employee details, hrm_platform_departments for department name (handle null), and hrm_platform_members for change author information.

Support cursor-based or offset pagination with configurable page size (default 20, max 100).

Support sorting by changed_at (descending default), created_at, employee_id.

Authorization: Require member actor with org:manage permission.

Return summary view with employee name, department name (or null indicator), changed_by name, changed_at timestamp.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of employee department assignment history summaries

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for filtering employee department history records

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific employee department history audit record by its unique identifier.

This operation returns detailed information about a single department assignment change event, including which employee was affected, which department they were assigned to (or null if removed from department), which member made the change, and when the change occurred.

Employee department histories are immutable audit records that provide a complete trail of organizational structure changes. Each record captures a point-in-time snapshot of a department assignment change, enabling compliance tracking and organizational audit requirements.

The response includes the employee reference, department reference (nullable), the member who initiated the change, and timestamps for both the change event and record creation. This data is essential for understanding organizational restructuring history and employee movement patterns within the organization.

Access to this endpoint requires appropriate permissions to view employee or organizational audit data. The operation enforces organization context isolation, ensuring users can only access history records within their current organization scope.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query the hrm_platform_employee_department_histories table by primary key id (UUID format). Join with hrm_platform_employees to include employee details, hrm_platform_departments for department information (left join since department_id is nullable), and hrm_platform_members for the user who made the change. Enforce organization context filtering to ensure data isolation - only return records belonging to the user's current organization. Validate that the historyId parameter is a valid UUID format. Return 404 if no record found with the given ID. Response should include all fields: id, employee_id, department_id (nullable), changed_by_id, changed_at, and created_at with proper ISO 8601 datetime formatting.

responseBody.description: Employee department history audit record with employee, department, and change metadata

parameters.description: Target employee department history record's unique identifier (UUID format)
parameters.name: historyId

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of roles within the current organization.

This operation provides search capabilities for viewing roles assigned to employees in the organization. The endpoint returns both built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) which are system-defined and cannot be deleted, as well as custom roles created by organization owners with specific permission sets.

Supports filtering by role name through partial text matching and by built-in status to distinguish between system roles and custom roles. Results are paginated with configurable page sizes and sorting options.

Access requires member authentication with appropriate permissions. Users with employee:view permission can view the role list, while users with org:manage or employee:manage permissions can perform additional role management operations.

The response includes role summary information optimized for list displays, containing the role ID, name, built-in flag, and creation timestamp. For detailed role information including assigned permissions, use the GET /roles/{roleId} endpoint.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query hrm_platform_roles table filtered by current organization_id from session context.

Apply search filters:
- name: partial text matching using LIKE operator with trigram index on display_name
- built_in: exact boolean match to filter built-in vs custom roles

Implement cursor-based pagination with limit and offset support.
Sort results by created_at descending by default, with optional sort field parameter.

Join with hrm_platform_role_permissions to count permission assignments if needed for summary.
Join with hrm_platform_employees to count assigned employees for display purposes.

Validate organization context from member session - roles are strictly isolated per organization.
Return IPageIHrmPlatformRole.ISummary with pagination metadata and role summary array.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of role summaries

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for role listing

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific role within the organization.

This operation returns complete role information including the role name, whether it is a built-in system role, and audit metadata. Built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) are protected system roles that cannot be deleted or modified, while custom roles can be managed by organization owners.

The role must belong to the authenticated user's organization. Access is restricted to member actors who are part of the organization. The operation queries the hrm_platform_roles table and returns all role attributes including the built_in flag that indicates if the role is a protected system role.

This endpoint is commonly used before performing role management operations such as editing custom roles or assigning roles to employees. The built_in field helps UI clients determine whether delete or edit actions should be enabled for the role.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query the hrm_platform_roles table by the provided roleId UUID parameter. Verify the role belongs to the authenticated user's current organization by checking organization_id matches the session context. Return the complete role record including id, organization_id, name, built_in flag, created_at, updated_at, and deleted_at fields. If the role does not exist or belongs to a different organization, return 404. If the role is soft-deleted (deleted_at is not null), return 404. No joins required as this is a simple single-table lookup. Authorization requires member actor with valid organization context.

responseBody.description: Complete role information including name, built-in status, and metadata

operations.description:
Create a new custom role within the organization.

This operation allows organization owners to define custom roles with specific permission sets tailored to their organizational needs. Custom roles supplement the three built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) that exist by default in every organization.

When creating a custom role, the user specifies a unique name and selects from available permissions including: org:manage, employee:manage, employee:view, project:manage, project:view, time:manage, time:approve, time:view_all, and report:view. The role name must be unique within the organization and cannot duplicate existing built-in or custom role names.

The created role is immediately available for assignment to employees. Employees assigned to the custom role inherit all permissions defined in the role's permission set. Permission changes to a custom role take effect immediately for all assigned employees.

This endpoint is restricted to organization owners and members with org:manage permission. The organization context is automatically derived from the authenticated user's session, ensuring proper data isolation.
operations.name: create
operations.specification: Query the authenticated user's current organization from session context. Validate the user has org:manage permission or is the organization owner. Check that the requested role name does not already exist in the organization (unique constraint on organization_id, name). Validate all permission codes are from the allowed set. Create the hrm_platform_roles record with built_in set to false. For each permission in the request, create corresponding hrm_platform_role_permissions records. Return the created role with its complete structure including id, timestamps, and permission assignments. Handle unique constraint violations with appropriate error messages indicating the role name already exists.

responseBody.description: The created custom role with all its properties

requestBody.description: Custom role creation data including name and permission set

operations.description:
Update an existing custom role's information within the organization.

This operation allows organization owners to modify custom role attributes, primarily the role name. The endpoint validates that the target role exists and belongs to the authenticated user's organization context.

Built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) are protected from modification. Attempts to update built-in roles will be rejected with an appropriate error response. The built_in flag on the hrm_platform_roles table indicates whether a role is system-defined and immutable.

Role names must be unique within an organization, enforced by the unique constraint on [organization_id, name]. If the new name conflicts with an existing role in the same organization, the operation fails with a constraint violation error.

This operation only updates the role's metadata (name). Permission assignments for custom roles are managed through the separate hrm_platform_role_permissions table via dedicated endpoints. To fully configure a custom role, use this endpoint for the name and the permissions endpoints for the permission set.

Users with org:manage or employee:manage permissions can access this endpoint. The organization context is derived from the authenticated session, ensuring data isolation between organizations.
operations.name: update
operations.specification: Query hrm_platform_roles table by roleId UUID. Validate role exists and is not soft deleted (deleted_at is null). Verify role.organization_id matches the authenticated user's current organization context. Check built_in flag - if true, reject the request with 403 Forbidden (built-in roles cannot be modified). Validate the new name is not empty and meets length requirements. Check for name uniqueness within the organization using the unique constraint. Update the name field and set updated_at to current timestamp. Return the updated IHrmPlatformRole object with all fields. Handle constraint violation errors with appropriate 409 Conflict response for duplicate names.

responseBody.description: Updated role information

requestBody.description: Update information for the custom role

prerequisites.description: Role must be created before it can be updated. This establishes the role entity in the database with a valid organization_id foreign key relationship.

operations.description:
Permanently remove a custom role from the organization through soft deletion.

This operation deletes a role by setting its deleted_at timestamp, effectively removing it from active use while preserving historical data. The endpoint enforces critical business rules to maintain organizational integrity and prevent data inconsistencies.

Built-in roles including Owner, Manager, and Employee are protected from deletion regardless of assignment status. The system validates the built_in flag and rejects any deletion attempt on system-defined roles with an appropriate error response indicating the role is a protected built-in role.

Custom roles can only be deleted when no employees are currently assigned to that role. Before deletion, the system checks the hrm_platform_employees table for any records referencing the target role. If active assignments exist, the operation is rejected with an error indicating employees must be reassigned to different roles before deletion can proceed.

This operation requires the caller to have organization management permissions (org:manage or equivalent Owner role access). The role must belong to the caller's current organization context, enforced through organization_id validation.

Upon successful deletion, the role's deleted_at field is populated with the current timestamp, and the role is excluded from all subsequent queries that filter out soft-deleted records. The operation returns no response body on success, following REST conventions for DELETE operations.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
1. Validate the roleId parameter is a valid UUID format.

2. Query hrm_platform_roles table to find the role by id, ensuring it belongs to the caller's organization (organization_id match) and is not already soft-deleted (deleted_at IS NULL).

3. If role not found, return 404 error.

4. Check if role.built_in is true. If true, reject with 403 Forbidden error indicating built-in roles cannot be deleted.

5. Query hrm_platform_employees table to count employees assigned to this role (role_id match) where employee is active (not deactivated).

6. If employee count > 0, reject with 409 Conflict error indicating employees are assigned to this role and must be reassigned before deletion.

7. Perform soft delete: UPDATE hrm_platform_roles SET deleted_at = CURRENT_TIMESTAMP WHERE id = roleId.

8. Create an activity log entry in hrm_platform_activity_logs recording the role deletion action with user reference, organization reference, action type, and role details.

9. Return 204 No Content response on success.

prerequisites.description: Role must be created before it can be deleted

operations.description:
Update the permission set for a custom role within an organization.

This operation allows organization owners to modify the permissions granted to a custom role by replacing the entire permission set with a new array of permission codes. The available permissions include: org:manage (edit organization settings), employee:manage (add/edit/deactivate employees), employee:view (view employee list), project:manage (create/edit/delete projects), project:view (view projects), time:manage (edit any timelog), time:approve (approve/reject timesheets), time:view_all (view all timelogs), and report:view (access organization reports).

This endpoint only works for custom roles where built_in is false. Attempting to update permissions on built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) will be rejected. The role must belong to the organization of the requesting user. Changes to a role's permissions take effect immediately for all employees currently assigned to that role.

The operation performs a complete replacement of the permission set. Any permissions not included in the request array are removed, and any new permissions in the array are added. The system validates that all provided permission codes are valid values from the allowed set. If the role has employees assigned to it, the permission changes apply to those employees immediately without requiring reassignment.

Access to this endpoint requires the user to be an organization owner with the org:manage permission. The operation returns the updated role object including its metadata but not the individual permission records. To retrieve the full permission set after update, use the GET /roles/{roleId} endpoint.
operations.name: updatePermissions
operations.specification:
1. Validate the roleId exists and is a valid UUID format.
2. Query hrm_platform_roles table to find the role by id.
3. Verify the role belongs to the authenticated user's organization (organization_id matches session context).
4. Check that built_in is false - reject if attempting to update built-in role permissions.
5. Validate the request body contains a valid array of permission codes from the allowed set: org:manage, employee:manage, employee:view, project:manage, project:view, time:manage, time:approve, time:view_all, report:view.
6. Begin database transaction.
7. Delete all existing permission records from hrm_platform_role_permissions where role_id matches the target role.
8. Insert new permission records for each permission code in the request array, creating one hrm_platform_role_permissions record per permission.
9. Commit the transaction.
10. Return the updated hrm_platform_roles record.
11. Log the action to hrm_platform_activity_logs with action type 'role.permissions.updated'.

Edge cases:
- Empty permission array: Valid, results in role with no permissions (though not recommended)
- Duplicate permissions in request: Deduplicate before inserting
- Invalid permission code: Return 400 Bad Request with list of valid codes
- Role not found: Return 404 Not Found
- Built-in role: Return 403 Forbidden
- User lacks org:manage permission: Return 403 Forbidden

responseBody.description: Updated role information

requestBody.description: New permission set for the role

prerequisites.description: Organization must be created before roles can be assigned to it, as roles belong to exactly one organization via organization_id foreign key
Custom role must be created before its permissions can be updated, as the operation requires a valid roleId that references an existing role record

operations.description:
Add a new permission to a custom role's permission set.

This operation creates a single permission assignment record linking a permission code to a custom role. Each permission grants specific access rights to employees assigned to that role. Available permissions include organization management, employee management and viewing, project management and viewing, time tracking management and approval, and report viewing capabilities.

The role must be a custom role created by the organization; built-in system roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) cannot have their permissions modified. The permission code must be one of the valid permission types defined in the system. Duplicate permission assignments for the same role are prevented by a unique constraint.

operations.description:
Create a new employment contract for a specific employee within the organization.

This operation allows users with employee management permission to establish or update employment terms for an employee. When a new contract is created, the system automatically manages the contract lifecycle by ending any previously active contract. If the employee has an existing contract without an end date (indicating it is ongoing), that contract's end date is automatically set to the day before the new contract's start date, ensuring only one contract is active at any time.

The contract requires a start date marking when the employment terms begin, a pay rate as a numeric value, a pay period classification (hourly, daily, weekly, or monthly), and working hours per week defining the expected weekly commitment. An optional end date can be specified for fixed-term contracts; contracts without an end date are considered ongoing. Optional notes field allows recording additional terms or conditions.

Authorization requires the employee:manage permission within the employee's organization. Employees can view their own contracts but cannot create contracts. Users with only employee:view permission can read contracts but cannot create or modify them. Past contracts become immutable historical records once superseded by a newer contract and cannot be edited regardless of permission level.

The operation validates that the pay period is one of the allowed values and that numeric fields (pay rate, working hours) are positive values. The start date must be provided and cannot be null. Upon successful creation, the complete contract object is returned including system-generated timestamps for created_at and updated_at.

If found, update that contract's end_date to be one day before the new contract's start_date within a database transaction. Insert the new contract record into hrm_platform_employee_contracts with all provided fields. The pay_period must be validated against allowed values: hourly, daily, weekly, monthly. The pay_rate must be a positive number. The working_hours_per_week must be a positive integer. The start_date is required. Return the complete newly created contract object including all fields and timestamps.

The start date cannot be changed as it marks when the contract terms began.

Access to this operation requires employee:manage permission within the organization. Employees can view their own contracts but cannot create or edit them. Users with only employee:view permission can view contracts but cannot modify them. - User must have employee:manage permission
- Contract must belong to the specified employee
