operations.description:
Soft delete a project from the organization by marking it as deleted.

This operation marks a project record as deleted by setting its deleted_at timestamp, effectively hiding it from active views while preserving all associated data. The deletion is subject to strict business rules: a project can only be deleted if it has no timelogs associated with it. This constraint ensures that historical time tracking data integrity is maintained and prevents accidental loss of work records.

Users with project management permissions (project:manage) can delete projects. If the project has one or more timelogs, the deletion request is rejected with an error indicating that projects with existing timelogs must be archived or completed instead. Projects without any timelogs can be deleted regardless of their current status (active, archived, or completed).

When a project is successfully soft deleted, the deleted_at timestamp is set and the project is no longer visible in active project lists. All tasks associated with that project remain in the database but are also hidden from active views. The operation preserves timelogs on other projects and maintains data consistency through the soft delete pattern.

Before attempting deletion, consider using the archive or complete status change operations if the project has timelogs but should be removed from active use. This preserves the historical data while achieving similar organizational goals.

Note: This operation performs a soft delete, not permanent removal. The project record remains in the database with a deleted_at timestamp and can potentially be recovered through administrative processes.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Delete a project by UUID identifier with timelog validation.

Implementation steps:
1. Validate user has project:manage permission in the organization context
2. Query hrm_platform_projects by projectId, ensuring it belongs to user's organization
3. Check for associated timelogs: query hrm_platform_timelogs where project_id equals projectId
4. If timelogs exist (count > 0), reject with 400 Bad Request error indicating project has time records
5. If no timelogs exist, perform cascading delete:
   - Delete all hrm_platform_tasks where project_id equals projectId (cascade handles this)
   - Delete the hrm_platform_projects record
6. Log the deletion action to hrm_platform_activity_logs with action type 'project_deleted'
7. Return 204 No Content on success

Edge cases:
- Project not found: return 404 Not Found
- User lacks permission: return 403 Forbidden
- Project has timelogs: return 400 Bad Request with descriptive error
- Project already soft-deleted: return 404 Not Found (treat as non-existent)

Database transactions: Wrap the timelog check and deletion in a transaction to prevent race conditions where timelogs might be added between check and delete.

9. Create new project_members record with: id (UUID), hrm_platform_employee_id, hrm_platform_project_id, role, created_at, updated_at
10. Log activity: record 'project_member_assigned' action in activity_logs with user, organization, target entity (project_member), and details (employee name, project name, role)
11. Return the created membership record with employee and project information joined

Edge cases:
- Employee already assigned to project: return 409 Conflict
- Employee is deactivated: return 400 Bad Request
- Project is archived or completed: still allow assignment (historical projects may need team members)
- User lacks project:manage permission: return 403 Forbidden

The employee will no longer be able to log time against this project or view tasks within it. However, all historical data including timelogs and task assignments made while the employee was a member are preserved for audit and reporting purposes.

The project membership uses soft deletion, meaning the record is marked with a deleted_at timestamp rather than being permanently removed from the database. This ensures complete audit trail for compliance and allows potential recovery if needed.

The task list supports flexible sorting by due date to show tasks with nearest or furthest deadlines first, by priority level to surface urgent tasks, or by creation date to show recently created or oldest tasks. Multiple sort criteria can be combined, such as sorting by priority first then by due date within each priority level.

Access is restricted to employees who are members of the project through hrm_platform_project_members assignment, or users with project management permission. operations.description:
Create a new task within a project.

This operation creates a new work item (task) within the specified project. Tasks are the fundamental units of work tracking in the HRM platform, supporting status workflow management, priority levels, time estimation, and optional assignment to team members.

The task creation requires the caller to be either a project lead (member with project-lead role in the project) or a user with project:manage permission. The assigned employee, if specified, must be a member of the project to ensure proper access control and workflow integrity.

Tasks support one-level parent-child hierarchy for subtask organization. A subtask references its parent task through the parent_id field. Subtasks cannot have their own children, enforcing a flat two-level structure. The parent task must belong to the same project as the new task.

Task status values (open, in-progress, completed, closed) define the workflow state. When a task is created with a status other than the default, the initial status is recorded in the task history audit trail. Priority levels (low, medium, high, urgent) enable task sorting and filtering for effective work queue management.

Related operations: PATCH /projects/{projectId}/tasks for listing tasks with filtering and pagination. GET /tasks/{taskId} for retrieving detailed task information. PUT /tasks/{taskId} for updating task attributes. POST /tasks/{taskId}/histories is automatically triggered when status changes occur.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new task record in the hrm_platform_tasks table with the following implementation logic:

1. Validate caller authorization: Check if the authenticated user is a project lead (has project membership with role='project-lead') OR has project:manage permission in the organization. Reject with 403 if neither condition is met.

2. Verify project existence and state: Query hrm_platform_projects by projectId. Ensure the project exists and is not soft-deleted. If project is archived or completed, creation may still be allowed but should be noted in business logic.

3. Validate assigned employee (if provided): If hrm_platform_employee_id is in the request, verify the employee exists, belongs to the same organization as the project, and is an active member of the project (exists in hrm_platform_project_members with the project). Reject with 400 if employee is not a project member.

4. Validate parent task (if provided): If parent_id is in the request, verify the parent task exists, belongs to the same project, is not soft-deleted, and does not itself have a parent (enforcing one-level nesting). Reject with 400 if parent has its own parent.

5. Validate status and priority values: Ensure status is one of ['open', 'in-progress', 'completed', 'closed'] and priority is one of ['low', 'medium', 'high', 'urgent']. Reject with 400 for invalid values.

6. Create task record: Insert into hrm_platform_tasks with all provided fields. Set created_at and updated_at to current timestamp. Set deleted_at to null.

7. Create initial task history: If status is provided (not default), create a record in hrm_platform_task_histories with old_status=null, new_status=provided status, user_id=caller's member_id, created_at=current timestamp.

8. Return the created task with full details including all fields and relationships.

responseBody.description: Created task with full details

Authorization is enforced at two levels: the user must be either a project lead (an employee with the project-lead role assignment in the hrm_platform_project_members table for this specific project) or possess the project:manage permission through their organizational role. The assigned employee, if specified, must be a member of the project to ensure proper access control.

Parent task relationships are limited to one level of nesting only. A subtask cannot have its own subtasks. The parent task, if provided, must belong to the same project as the task being updated. Tasks in archived or completed projects cannot have their status changed to open or in-progress, preserving project lifecycle integrity.

This operation complements the task creation endpoint (POST /projects/{projectId}/tasks) and the task retrieval endpoint (GET /projects/{projectId}/tasks/{taskId}). For listing tasks with filtering and pagination, use PATCH /projects/{projectId}/tasks.

Each history entry captures the timestamp when the change occurred, the previous status before the change, the new status after the change, and the user who made the status change. Task history records are automatically generated by the system whenever a task status is modified through task editing or any other operation that changes the status.

The endpoint enforces organizational data isolation by requiring both the project ID and task ID in the path. This ensures that users can only access task histories for tasks within projects they have permission to view. The system validates that the specified task belongs to the specified project before returning any results.

Supports comprehensive filtering and pagination capabilities. Users can filter history records by date range to view status changes within specific time periods, filter by user to see changes made by specific team members, and filter by old or new status values to track specific transitions. Results are sorted by creation timestamp in descending order by default, showing the most recent status changes first.

This operation is read-only. Task history entries cannot be created, modified, or deleted through the API as they are system-generated audit records that ensure complete tracking of all status changes for compliance and workflow management purposes.

The response includes timelogs regardless of their timesheet approval status, though timelogs in approved timesheets are locked from modification.

Results are sorted by date in descending order by default, showing the most recent time entries first. The endpoint supports cursor-based pagination for efficient browsing of large timelog collections.

The employee_id references the hrm_platform_employees table, project_id references hrm_platform_projects, task_id optionally references hrm_platform_tasks, and timesheet_id optionally references hrm_platform_timesheets. operations.description:
Create a new timelog entry to record work performed by an employee.

This operation allows employees to create individual time entries capturing discrete units of work. Each timelog represents work performed on a specific date with a defined duration, assigned to a project and optionally linked to a specific task within that project.

The system automatically associates the timelog with the authenticated employee - no employee identifier is required in the request body. The employee must be assigned to the specified project as a project member. If a task is provided, it must belong to the selected project.

Timelogs include a work date (when the work was performed, not when the entry was created), duration in minutes (must be positive), an optional description of the work performed, and a billable flag indicating whether the time is chargeable to the client.

The system enforces timesheet constraints: timelogs cannot be created for dates that fall within an already approved timesheet week for this employee. If a draft timesheet exists for the week, the timelog will be automatically included. Timelogs cannot be created for projects with status archived or completed.

Related operations: PATCH /timelogs for listing timelogs with filters, GET /timelogs/{timelogId} for retrieving a specific timelog, PUT /timelogs/{timelogId} for updating an existing timelog, DELETE /timelogs/{timelogId} for removing a timelog.
operations.name: create

Insert a new record into hrm_platform_timelogs table with the provided data.

Validation steps:
1. Verify employee_id matches authenticated user's employee record (or user has time:manage permission for other employees)
2. Verify project exists and employee is assigned to it via hrm_platform_project_members
3. If task_id provided, verify task exists and belongs to the specified project
4. Verify the date does not fall within an approved timesheet week for this employee
5. Validate duration_minutes is a positive integer
6. Set created_at and updated_at to current timestamp
7. Set deleted_at to null

Business logic:
- If a draft timesheet exists for the week containing this date, automatically associate the timelog with that timesheet
- Calculate week boundaries (Monday to Sunday) in the organization's timezone
- Trigger activity log entry if this is a significant action
- Return the complete created timelog entity with all relationships loaded

Update an existing timelog record with new work details.

Employees can only update their own timelogs. Users with the time:manage permission can update any timelog within their organization. When updating the task_id, the system validates that the task belongs to the selected project. When updating the project_id, the system validates that the employee is assigned to that project.

If the timelog is included in a submitted or approved timesheet, the update request is rejected. This ensures that approved time records cannot be modified after approval, maintaining audit trail integrity.

The operation performs full field replacement - all provided fields in the request body overwrite the existing values. Fields not included in the request body remain unchanged. The updated_at timestamp is automatically updated to reflect the modification time.

operations.description:
Permanently remove a time entry record from the system.

This operation deletes a specific timelog identified by its UUID. Timelogs represent individual work sessions logged by employees, including date, duration, project assignment, and optional task reference. Deletion is subject to authorization rules and timesheet status constraints to maintain data integrity.

Authorization is enforced at two levels. Employees can delete their own timelogs only when the timelog is not part of a submitted or approved timesheet. Users with the time:manage permission can delete any employee's timelogs regardless of timesheet status, providing administrative override capability. This ensures that time tracking data included in approved timesheets remains protected from accidental modification while allowing authorized administrators to correct errors when necessary.

The deletion process performs a soft delete by setting the deleted_at timestamp, preserving the record for audit purposes while removing it from active queries. Before deletion, the system validates that the timelog exists, checks the authenticated user's permissions against the timelog's employee ownership, and verifies the associated timesheet status if one exists. Timelogs without timesheet assignment or in draft timesheets can be freely deleted by their owners.

Related operations include PATCH /timelogs for retrieving timelog lists with filtering capabilities, and GET /timelogs/{timelogId} for viewing individual timelog details before deletion. After successful deletion, the timelog will no longer appear in list queries or detail retrievals.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Delete a timelog record from hrm_platform_timelogs table by UUID.

Authorization flow:
1. Authenticate user as member actor
2. Retrieve timelog by timelogId
3. If user has time:manage permission → allow deletion
4. Else if timelog.employee_id matches authenticated user's employee record → proceed to step 5
5. Check timesheet status: if timelog.timesheet_id exists, load timesheet and verify status is not 'submitted' or 'approved'
6. If timelog is in submitted/approved timesheet and user lacks time:manage permission → reject with 403
7. Perform soft delete by setting deleted_at timestamp
8. Return 204 No Content

Business validations:
- Timelog must exist and not be already deleted
- Employees can only delete their own timelogs
- Timelogs in submitted timesheets cannot be deleted by employees
- Timelogs in approved timesheets cannot be deleted by employees
- Users with time:manage permission bypass timesheet status restrictions

Edge cases:
- Timelog with null timesheet_id → can be deleted by owner
- Timelog in draft timesheet → can be deleted by owner
- Non-existent timelogId → return 404
- Already deleted timelog → return 404

prerequisites.description: Employee must exist to own the timelog being deleted
Project must exist as timelogs must be assigned to a project
Employee must be assigned to the project before creating timelogs for that project
Timelog must be created before it can be deleted

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of timesheet records.

This endpoint provides comprehensive timesheet listing capabilities for time tracking management. Employees can access their own timesheets to monitor submission and approval status throughout the weekly workflow cycle. Users with timesheet approval permissions can view all timesheets across the organization for review and audit purposes.

The operation supports multiple filtering dimensions including timesheet status filtering to isolate drafts, submitted, approved, or rejected timesheets. Date range filtering enables retrieval of timesheets for specific periods, supporting historical analysis and reporting requirements. Pagination parameters allow efficient browsing of large timesheet histories.

Access control is enforced based on user permissions: regular employees are restricted to their own timesheets only, while users with time:approve or time:view_all permissions can access the complete organizational timesheet dataset. This ensures data isolation while enabling appropriate oversight capabilities.

The response includes timesheet summary information optimized for list displays, containing essential fields such as week period, status, total hours, submission timestamp, and review status. Detailed timesheet information with full timelog breakdowns can be retrieved through the detail endpoint.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query hrm_platform_timesheets table with pagination and filtering support.

Apply status filter when provided to match draft, submitted, approved, or rejected states. Apply date range filtering on week_start_date and week_end_date fields when range parameters are provided.

Enforce access control: if user lacks time:approve or time:view_all permission, filter results to only include timesheets owned by the requesting employee. Join with hrm_platform_employees to verify ownership.

Return paginated results with cursor-based or offset-based pagination. Include pagination metadata (total count, page info) in response.

Sort results by week_start_date descending by default to show most recent timesheets first. Support custom sorting if specified in request.

Handle edge cases: empty result sets return empty data array with pagination metadata. Invalid status values return validation error. Date range with end before start returns validation error.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of timesheet summaries

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for timesheet filtering

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific timesheet by its unique identifier.

This operation returns detailed information about a single timesheet record, including the weekly period it covers (week_start_date to week_end_date), current workflow status (draft, submitted, approved, or rejected), submission and review timestamps, and rejection reason if applicable.

Authorization is enforced based on timesheet ownership and user permissions. Employees can only access their own timesheets, while users with time:view_all or time:approve permissions can view any timesheet across the organization. This ensures data isolation and privacy between employees while allowing authorized reviewers to access timesheets for approval workflows.

The response includes all timesheet fields: employee ownership reference, optional reviewer reference, week period dates, status, submitted_at timestamp, reviewed_at timestamp, rejection_reason (when status is rejected), and audit timestamps (created_at, updated_at, deleted_at).

Related operations: PATCH /timesheets for listing timesheets with filtering and pagination, PUT /timesheets/{timesheetId} for updating timesheet details, POST /timesheets/{timesheetId}/approve for approving submitted timesheets, POST /timesheets/{timesheetId}/reject for rejecting timesheets with reason.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query the hrm_platform_timesheets table by primary key (timesheetId UUID).

Authorization check:
- If user has time:view_all or time:approve permission: allow access to any timesheet
- Otherwise: verify timesheet.employee_id matches the authenticated employee's ID
- Reject with 403 Forbidden if authorization fails

Join with hrm_platform_employees to include employee information if needed in response.
Join with hrm_platform_members to include reviewer information if reviewed_by_id is not null.

Return 404 Not Found if timesheet doesn't exist or is soft-deleted (deleted_at is not null).

Ensure soft-deleted records are excluded from results by filtering where deleted_at IS NULL.

responseBody.description: Detailed timesheet information including week period, status, and review details

operations.description:
Create a new timesheet for the authenticated employee.

This operation creates a weekly timesheet record in draft status, allowing employees to begin tracking and organizing their work hours for a specific week period. The timesheet covers a standard Monday-to-Sunday week, with the week_start_date parameter defining the beginning of the period.

The employee creating the timesheet becomes the owner (employee_id) and has full control over the draft timesheet, including adding timelogs, submitting for approval, or deleting the draft. Each employee can have only one timesheet per week, enforced by the unique constraint on employee_id and week_start_date.

Upon successful creation, the timesheet is initialized with 'draft' status, allowing the employee to add timelog entries before submission. The week_end_date is automatically calculated as week_start_date plus 6 days (Sunday). Submitted and reviewed timestamps are null until the timesheet progresses through the approval workflow.

Users with time:manage or time:approve permissions can create timesheets on behalf of other employees by specifying the employee context. This supports administrative workflows where managers assist with timesheet creation.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new hrm_platform_timesheets record with the following implementation logic:

1. Validate the requesting user has member actor status and appropriate permissions (time:manage, time:approve, or is creating for themselves)

2. Extract week_start_date from request body and calculate week_end_date as week_start_date + 6 days

3. Check unique constraint: query hrm_platform_timesheets for existing record with same employee_id and week_start_date. If found, return conflict error indicating timesheet already exists for that week

4. Create timesheet record with:
   - employee_id: authenticated employee's ID (or specified employee if admin)
   - week_start_date: from request body
   - week_end_date: calculated as week_start_date + 6 days
   - status: 'draft'
   - submitted_at: null
   - reviewed_by_id: null
   - reviewed_at: null
   - rejection_reason: null
   - created_at: current timestamp
   - updated_at: current timestamp
   - deleted_at: null

5. Return the complete IHrmPlatformTimesheet entity including all fields

6. Handle edge cases:
   - Duplicate week: return 409 Conflict with message about existing timesheet
   - Invalid date format: return 400 Bad Request
   - Insufficient permissions: return 403 Forbidden

responseBody.description: Created timesheet entity with complete information

requestBody.description: Timesheet creation information including week start date

prerequisites.description: Employee record must exist before creating a timesheet because the timesheet's employee_id is derived from the authenticated member's organizational membership. The employee record establishes the link between the member account and the organization with role assignment.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of timer records for the authenticated employee.

This operation provides search capabilities for timer sessions including filtering by running status (active vs stopped), project association, task assignment, and date ranges. Employees can use this endpoint to view their current running timer as well as historical timer sessions.

The endpoint enforces organization data isolation, returning only timers belonging to the authenticated user's employee record within their current organization context. Each employee can have at most one active timer at any time, but may have multiple historical stopped timers.

Supports comprehensive pagination with configurable page sizes and sorting options. Response includes timer summary information optimized for list displays, showing start time, project, optional task, description, and current status.

Related operations include GET /timers/{timerId} for detailed timer information, PUT /timers/{timerId} for updating a running timer, POST /timers for starting a new timer, and DELETE /timers/{timerId} for discarding a timer without creating a timelog.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query hrm_platform_timers table with pagination and filtering support.

Apply search filters on: stopped_at (null for running, not null for stopped), project_id, task_id, started_at date range, description text search.

Join with hrm_platform_projects to include project name in summary.
Left join with hrm_platform_tasks to include task name when present.
Filter by employee_id from authenticated session context.
Apply organization isolation through employee's organization_id.
Return cursor-based or offset pagination with total count.
Sort by started_at descending by default (most recent first).

Handle edge case where employee has no timers (return empty array with pagination metadata).
Ensure soft-deleted timers (deleted_at not null) are excluded from results.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of timer summaries

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for timer list query

operations.description:
Retrieve detailed information about a specific timer session by its identifier.

This operation returns the complete timer record including the start timestamp when tracking began, the associated project being tracked, the optional task within the project, and the optional description of work being performed. If the timer has been stopped, the stopped_at timestamp is included to enable duration calculation.

Only the employee who owns the timer can access this endpoint. The system validates that the requesting employee matches the timer's employee_id field, ensuring strict data isolation between organization members.

The response includes all timer attributes necessary for displaying elapsed time calculations in the user interface. Clients can use the started_at timestamp to compute real-time elapsed duration since the timer began.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query the hrm_platform_timers table by the provided timerId UUID parameter. Validate that the timer exists and has not been soft deleted (deleted_at is null). Verify that the authenticated employee's ID matches the timer's employee_id field to enforce ownership access control. Return the complete timer record including id, employee_id, project_id, task_id (nullable), started_at, stopped_at (nullable), description (nullable), created_at, and updated_at fields. Join with hrm_platform_projects to include project details if needed for the response DTO. Join with hrm_platform_tasks if task_id is present to include task details. Handle 404 Not Found if timer doesn't exist or employee doesn't have access. Handle 403 Forbidden if timer belongs to a different employee.

responseBody.description: Timer session details with project and optional task information

operations.description:
Create a new timer session for real-time time tracking.

This operation initiates a live timer session that allows employees to track work duration in real-time. The employee must select a project they are assigned to, and can optionally specify a task within that project and provide a description of the work being performed.

The system enforces that each employee can have at most one active timer at any given time. If the employee already has a running timer, the request will be rejected. The timer records the start timestamp when created and continues running indefinitely until manually stopped or discarded by the employee.

While the timer is running, employees can edit the description, change the selected project, or change the task. When stopped, the timer converts to a timelog entry with the calculated duration rounded to the nearest minute. Alternatively, employees can discard the timer without creating any timelog record.

This endpoint is accessible only to authenticated member actors who are employees within an organization. The employee_id is automatically derived from the authenticated session context.
operations.name: create
operations.specification:
Create a new timer record in the hrm_platform_timers table with the following implementation logic:

1. Validate that the authenticated employee exists and is active
2. Check if the employee already has an active timer (stopped_at IS NULL and deleted_at IS NULL)
3. If active timer exists, reject with 409 Conflict error
4. Validate that the provided project_id exists and the employee is assigned to that project (via hrm_platform_project_members)
5. If task_id is provided, validate it exists and belongs to the specified project
6. Create the timer record with:
   - employee_id: from authenticated session
   - project_id: from request body
   - task_id: from request body (nullable)
   - started_at: current timestamp
   - stopped_at: null
   - description: from request body (nullable)
   - created_at: current timestamp
   - updated_at: current timestamp
   - deleted_at: null
7. Return the created timer object with full details

Transaction scope: Single table insert with validation queries. No complex transaction needed.

responseBody.description: The created timer session with all details

requestBody.description: Timer creation information including required project and optional task and description

operations.description:
Update an active timer's properties during a time tracking session.

This operation allows employees to modify their running timer's description, project assignment, and optional task association. Employees can edit these properties independently or together while the timer is actively running. The project must be from the employee's assigned projects, and if a task is specified, it must belong to the selected project.

This endpoint supports real-time adjustments to time tracking sessions, enabling employees to correct or refine their timer details as work context changes. The started_at timestamp and employee ownership cannot be modified. Only the timer owner (the employee who started the timer) can perform this update.

Related operations include GET /timers/{timerId} for retrieving timer details, POST /timers for starting a new timer, and DELETE /timers/{timerId} for discarding a timer without creating a timelog.
operations.name: update
operations.specification: Query hrm_platform_timers table by timerId UUID. Verify timer exists and belongs to the authenticated employee (employee_id matches session context). Validate timer is not already stopped (stopped_at is null) - reject if timer is stopped. Validate project_id exists in hrm_platform_projects and employee is assigned to that project via hrm_platform_project_members. If task_id is provided, validate it exists in hrm_platform_tasks and belongs to the selected project (project_id matches). Update description, project_id, and task_id fields atomically. Update updated_at timestamp to current time. Return complete updated timer record. Handle concurrent update conflicts with optimistic locking on updated_at if needed.

responseBody.description: Updated timer information with modified properties

requestBody.description: Updatable timer properties for modification

prerequisites.description: Project must be created before a timer can reference it, as timer creation requires a valid project_id from the employee's assigned projects
Timer must be created and be in running state before it can be updated - the timerId path parameter references an existing timer session
Task must exist before being referenced in timer update, and must belong to the selected project as validated by the update operation

operations.description:
Discard a running timer without creating a timelog entry.

This operation allows employees to discard their active timer sessions when they started tracking by mistake or no longer need to track time. Discarding a timer permanently removes the timer record without saving any time tracking data.

The timer must belong to the requesting employee. Only employees can discard their own timers. This operation implements soft deletion, marking the timer as deleted while preserving audit trail.

After discarding, the employee is immediately free to start a new timer. The discard action is irreversible and no record of the tracked time is preserved.

Related operations: POST /timers to start a new timer, GET /timers/{timerId} to view timer details before discarding.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Delete the timer record by setting deleted_at timestamp.

1. Verify timer exists and is not already deleted
2. Verify the timer belongs to the authenticated employee (employee_id matches)
3. Perform soft delete by setting deleted_at to current timestamp
4. Return 204 No Content on success

Business rules:
- Only the timer owner can discard their timer
- Discarding does not create a timelog entry
- Operation is irreversible
- Frees the employee to start a new timer immediately

Edge cases:
- Timer not found: return 404
- Timer belongs to different employee: return 403
- Timer already deleted: return 404

prerequisites.description: Timer must be created before it can be discarded. This prerequisite ensures a valid timer resource exists for the delete operation to target.

operations.description:
Submit a draft timesheet for approval review.

This operation transitions a timesheet from draft status to submitted status, initiating the approval workflow. The employee who owns the timesheet can submit it once they have completed logging all time entries for the week. Upon submission, the timesheet becomes locked and the employee can no longer modify the timesheet or its included timelogs until it is either approved or rejected by a reviewer.

The system performs several validation checks before allowing submission. First, the timesheet must contain at least one timelog entry - empty timesheets cannot be submitted. Second, there must not be another timesheet for the same employee and week period that is already in submitted or approved status. Third, the timesheet must currently be in draft status - already submitted timesheets cannot be resubmitted.

When submission succeeds, the system updates the timesheet status from draft to submitted and records the submission timestamp in the submitted_at field. The timesheet remains in submitted status until a reviewer with time:approve permission either approves or rejects it. This operation is typically followed by GET /timesheets/{timesheetId} to retrieve the updated timesheet state or PATCH /timesheets to list all timesheets for the employee.

Only the employee who owns the timesheet can submit it. Users with employee:manage or time:approve permissions may have separate endpoints for approving or rejecting submitted timesheets.
operations.name: submit
operations.specification:
Implement timesheet submission workflow with comprehensive validation.

1. Retrieve the timesheet by timesheetId from hrm_platform_timesheets table
2. Validate the requesting user is the owner (employee_id matches authenticated employee)
3. Validate timesheet status is 'draft' - reject if already submitted, approved, or rejected
4. Query hrm_platform_timelogs to count timelogs belonging to this timesheet
5. Validate at least one timelog exists - reject with error if timesheet is empty
6. Query for duplicate timesheets: same employee_id, same week_start_date, status in ('submitted', 'approved')
7. Validate no duplicate exists - reject if another timesheet for same week is already submitted or approved
8. Begin database transaction
9. Update timesheet: set status='submitted', submitted_at=current timestamp
10. Commit transaction
11. Return updated timesheet entity with full details

Error handling:
- 404: Timesheet not found
- 403: User is not the timesheet owner
- 400: Timesheet is not in draft status
- 400: Timesheet contains no timelogs
- 409: Duplicate timesheet exists for same week
- 400: Employee is deactivated (cannot submit timesheets)

Authorization: member actor who owns the timesheet (employee.user_id matches authenticated user)

responseBody.description: Updated timesheet with submitted status

prerequisites.description: Employee must be created and active before owning a timesheet. Deactivated employees cannot submit timesheets per business rules.
Timesheet must be created in draft status before it can be submitted for approval. The timesheetId path parameter references this created resource.
At least one timelog must be added to the timesheet. Empty timesheets cannot be submitted per validation rules in section 197.

operations.description:
Approve a submitted timesheet, transitioning it to approved status and locking all associated timelogs.

This operation allows users with time:approve permission to review and approve timesheets that are in submitted status. When a timesheet is approved, the system records the reviewer's identity in the reviewed_by_id field and sets the reviewed_at timestamp to the current time. The timesheet status changes from submitted to approved.

Approving a timesheet has a critical side effect: all timelog entries included in that timesheet become permanently locked, preventing any future edits or deletions. This ensures the integrity of approved time records for payroll and billing purposes.

The operation validates that the timesheet exists, is in submitted status, and the user has the required time:approve permission. If the timesheet is in draft, approved, or rejected status, the request is rejected with an appropriate error indicating the current status.

This operation is part of the timesheet approval workflow. Users typically retrieve the list of submitted timesheets first using PATCH /timesheets with status filter, then approve individual timesheets using this endpoint. After approval, the timesheet can be retrieved via GET /timesheets/{timesheetId} to confirm the updated status.
operations.name: approve
operations.specification:
Query the hrm_platform_timesheets table by the provided timesheetId path parameter.

Validate the following preconditions:
1. Timesheet exists and is not soft deleted (deleted_at is null)
2. Timesheet status is 'submitted' - reject if draft, approved, or rejected
3. Current user has time:approve permission in the organization context
4. Timesheet belongs to the current organization (via employee_id join)

If validation passes, execute an update transaction:
- Set status to 'approved'
- Set reviewed_by_id to current user's member ID
- Set reviewed_at to current timestamp
- Ensure rejection_reason is null

The timelog locking is enforced at the timelog level - when querying or updating timelogs, check if their parent timesheet is in approved status and reject modification attempts.

Return the updated timesheet record with all fields including the new reviewed_by_id and reviewed_at values.

Error handling:
- 404: Timesheet not found or soft deleted
- 400: Timesheet not in submitted status (include current status in error details)
- 403: User lacks time:approve permission

responseBody.description: Updated timesheet with approved status and review metadata

operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated time tracking statistics for organizational reporting and analysis.

This operation provides comprehensive time report generation by querying timelog entries across the organization. Users can filter results by date range, specific employees, projects, tasks, and billable status to generate targeted time reports for analysis, billing, or resource planning purposes.

The endpoint supports flexible grouping options allowing aggregation by employee, project, task, or date dimension. Each grouped result includes total hours logged, entry count, and billable/non-billable breakdowns. This enables managers and report viewers to analyze time allocation patterns, track project budget utilization, and review employee productivity.

Access requires the report:view permission. All results are scoped to the user's organization context ensuring data isolation. The response includes summary statistics optimized for report display and export workflows.

Related operations: GET /projects/{projectId} for project details, GET /employees/{employeeId} for employee information, PATCH /timesheets for timesheet data.
operations.name: search
operations.specification: Query hrm_platform_timelogs table with aggregation and filtering. Apply date range filter on timelog date field. Filter by employee_id, project_id, task_id if provided. Filter by billable flag if specified. Group results by requested dimension (employee, project, task, or date). Join with hrm_platform_employees for employee names, hrm_platform_projects for project names, hrm_platform_tasks for task titles. Calculate total duration_minutes per group, convert to hours. Return aggregated statistics with grouping dimension values. Ensure organization isolation by filtering timelogs through employee's organization_id. Validate that requesting user has report:view permission in their role.

responseBody.description: Aggregated time report statistics grouped by requested dimension

requestBody.description: Time report search criteria including date range, entity filters, and grouping options

operations.description:
Retrieve project budget utilization reports with budget hours versus actual hours comparison.

This operation provides comprehensive project budget tracking by comparing planned budget hours against actual logged hours. The report calculates budget consumption percentage for each project, enabling managers and owners to monitor project financial health and identify projects exceeding budget thresholds.

The endpoint requires report:view permission and returns paginated results with filtering capabilities. Users can filter by date range to analyze specific periods, by project status to focus on active or completed projects, and by budget utilization thresholds to identify at-risk projects. The report aggregates timelog data from the hrm_platform_timelogs table, joining with hrm_platform_projects to compute actual hours spent.

Projects with budget_hours set to null are excluded from percentage calculations but included in the report with actual hours only. The response includes project identification details (name, color code, status) alongside budget metrics for quick visual assessment in dashboard views.

This report is commonly used together with the time report endpoint to correlate budget consumption with team productivity. Organization dashboard displays projects over 80% budget utilization as a key metric, which can be obtained by filtering this endpoint with appropriate thresholds.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query hrm_platform_projects table joining with hrm_platform_timelogs to calculate actual hours per project.

Filter projects by organization_id from session context. Apply date range filter on timelogs.date for actual hours calculation. Filter by project status if provided. Calculate budget consumption percentage as (actual_hours / budget_hours) * 100.

Handle projects with null budget_hours by setting utilization_percentage to null. Group timelogs by project_id and sum duration_minutes, converting to hours (divide by 60).

Apply pagination with cursor-based or offset-based approach. Sort by utilization_percentage descending by default to surface over-budget projects first. Support sorting by project name, budget_hours, actual_hours, and utilization_percentage.

Ensure only users with report:view permission (Manager, Owner, or custom roles with report:view) can access this endpoint. Filter results to organization context from authenticated user's session.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of project budget utilization summaries

requestBody.description: Budget report search criteria and pagination parameters

operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated weekly summary reports showing time tracking statistics organized by week.

This operation provides week-by-week summaries including total hours worked, number of timelog entries, and count of active employees for each week. The weekly period follows Monday-Sunday boundaries based on the organization's timezone setting.

Supports filtering by date range to retrieve specific time periods and by project to focus on specific work initiatives. Results are returned in descending chronological order with the most recent weeks first.

Requires report:view permission to access organization reports. Response includes pagination support for navigating through historical weekly data spanning multiple months or years.

Related operations: PATCH /reports/time for detailed time reports with employee/project/task breakdowns, PATCH /reports/project-budget for budget utilization reports.
operations.name: search
operations.specification: Query hrm_platform_timelogs table with date range filtering to calculate weekly aggregations. Group timelogs by week (Monday-Sunday) based on work_date field. For each week, calculate: total duration (sum of minutes converted to hours), timelog count (count of entries), and employee count (count of distinct employee_id values). Apply project filter by joining with hrm_platform_projects if projectCode is provided in request. Ensure organization context is applied by joining timelogs with hrm_platform_employees to filter by organization_id. Return weeks in descending order (most recent first). Support pagination for historical data spanning many weeks. Handle timezone conversion using organization's timezone setting for week boundary calculations.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of weekly summary statistics with total hours, timelog counts, and employee counts per week

requestBody.description: Search criteria for weekly summary report including date range and optional project filter

operations.description:
Retrieve the authenticated employee's personal dashboard with aggregated time tracking statistics and work overview.

This endpoint compiles a comprehensive view of the employee's current work status by querying multiple data sources. The dashboard provides real-time insights into time logged today and this week, active timer sessions, recent time entries, pending timesheet approval status, and assigned tasks requiring attention.

The hours today metric sums all timelog durations for the current date in the user's timezone (Asia/Seoul). Hours this week aggregates timelogs from Monday through Sunday of the current week. These calculations exclude timelogs from deleted or archived projects.

The active timer section returns the currently running timer if one exists, including the associated project, optional task, start timestamp, and work description. Returns null when no timer is active.

Recent timelogs displays the five most recent time entries with project and task context, enabling quick review of recent work activity. Timelogs are ordered by date descending.

The pending timesheet section shows the current week's timesheet status, which may be draft (being built), submitted (awaiting approval), approved (locked), or rejected (requires correction). If rejected, the rejection reason is included to guide resubmission.

Assigned tasks lists all open and in-progress tasks assigned to the employee across their accessible projects, sorted by due date and priority. This helps employees prioritize their workload.

Access is restricted to member actors within their organization context. The employee's organization membership is determined from their authentication session.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query multiple tables to compile personal dashboard statistics for the authenticated employee.

1. Hours Today: Sum duration_minutes from hrm_platform_timelogs where employee_id matches current user and date = current date (Asia/Seoul timezone).

2. Hours This Week: Sum duration_minutes from hrm_platform_timelogs where employee_id matches and date is within current week (Monday 00:00 to Sunday 23:59 in Asia/Seoul timezone).

3. Active Timer: Query hrm_platform_timers where employee_id matches and stopped_at is null. Return timer with project, task, started_at, and description.

4. Recent Timelogs: Query hrm_platform_timelogs where employee_id matches, ordered by date DESC, limit 5. Include project name, task title, duration, date, billable flag.

5. Pending Timesheet: Query hrm_platform_timesheets where employee_id matches and week_start_date = current week's Monday. Return status (draft/submitted/approved/rejected), total hours, rejection_reason if rejected.

6. Assigned Tasks: Query hrm_platform_tasks where hrm_platform_employee_id matches and status in ('open', 'in-progress'). Include task title, project name, priority, due_date, status.

All queries must respect organization context - employee record determines which organization's data to access. Return null for sections with no data (e.g., no active timer, no pending timesheet).

responseBody.description: Personal dashboard with aggregated statistics and work overview

requestBody.description: Optional filters and sections to include in the dashboard response

operations.description:
Retrieve organization dashboard statistics and metrics for the current organization context.

This operation provides a comprehensive overview of organizational performance including workforce metrics, time tracking statistics, and project health indicators. The dashboard displays total active employees (from hrm_platform_employees where status is 'active'), total hours logged this week (aggregated from hrm_platform_timelogs.duration_minutes), pending timesheets awaiting approval (from hrm_platform_timesheets where status is 'submitted'), projects with budget utilization over 80 percent (from hrm_platform_projects comparing actual hours to budget_hours), and the top 5 employees by hours logged this week.

Access to this endpoint requires the report:view permission as defined in the organization's role-based access control. Users without this permission cannot access organization-level reports and dashboards. The data is strictly isolated per organization - users can only see dashboard data for their currently selected organization context from the session.

The response includes aggregated statistics computed from multiple data sources: hrm_platform_employees for workforce counts, hrm_platform_timelogs for time tracking data, hrm_platform_timesheets for approval workflow status, and hrm_platform_projects for budget utilization metrics. All queries are scoped to the organization_id from the user's session context to enforce multi-tenant data isolation.

Related operations include PATCH /dashboard/personal for individual employee dashboard data, which is accessible to all employees regardless of report:view permission. For detailed employee lists, use PATCH /employees. For detailed timesheet data, use PATCH /timesheets.
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query and aggregate data from multiple tables to compute organization dashboard statistics.

1. Validate user has report:view permission in current organization context
2. Retrieve total count of active employees from hrm_platform_employees where status is active
3. Calculate total hours logged this week by summing timelog durations from hrm_platform_timelogs for current week (Monday-Sunday based on organization timezone)
4. Count pending timesheets from hrm_platform_timesheets where status is 'submitted' or 'approved' awaiting review
5. Query hrm_platform_projects to find projects where actual hours exceed 80% of budget_hours
6. Retrieve top 5 employees by hours logged this week with their total hours
7. Apply date range filters from request body if provided (default to current week)
8. Return aggregated dashboard data as IHrmPlatformOrganizationDashboard

Ensure all queries are scoped to the current organization ID from session context for data isolation.

responseBody.description: Organization dashboard statistics including workforce metrics (total active employees), time tracking data (total hours logged this week, top 5 employees by hours), approval workflow status (pending timesheets count), and project health indicators (projects over 80% budget utilization).

requestBody.description: Optional filters for customizing dashboard date range and metrics. Includes week_start_date and week_end_date for custom reporting periods. If not provided, defaults to current week (Monday to Sunday) based on organization timezone.

operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of activity log entries for audit trail review.

This operation provides comprehensive search capabilities for organizational activity logs, allowing filtering by action type, member who performed the action, target entity type, and date ranges. Activity logs are automatically generated by the system when significant actions occur such as employee lifecycle events, contract changes, project operations, task status changes, timesheet workflow actions, and role assignments.

Only members with org:manage permission can access this endpoint. The response includes summarized activity log information optimized for list displays, with pagination support for large result sets. Results are scoped to the user's current organization context to ensure data isolation.

Filters support multiple action types, date range queries using created_at timestamps, and member-based filtering. The endpoint is commonly used for compliance audits, forensic analysis, and organizational activity monitoring.
operations.name: index
operations.specification:
Query hrm_platform_activity_logs table with pagination and filtering.
Apply search filters on action_type, member_id, target_entity_type, target_entity_id, and created_at date range.
Enforce organization context by filtering on organization_id from user's session.
Verify user has org:manage permission before executing query.
Join with hrm_platform_members table to include member information if needed.
Support cursor-based or offset pagination for large result sets.
Sort results by created_at DESC by default to show most recent activities first.
Return IPageIHrmPlatformActivityLog.ISummary with pagination metadata and data array.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of activity log summaries

requestBody.description: Search criteria and pagination parameters for activity log filtering

operations.description:
Retrieve a specific activity log entry by its unique identifier.

This operation provides access to detailed information about a single recorded organizational action. Activity logs capture significant events including employee lifecycle changes, contract modifications, project operations, task status changes, timesheet workflow transitions, and role assignments. Each entry includes the member who performed the action, the organization context, action type classification, target entity information, and additional contextual details.

Access to this endpoint requires organization management permissions (org:manage). The system enforces strict data isolation, ensuring users can only access activity logs from their currently selected organization context. This prevents cross-organization data exposure even when users belong to multiple organizations.

The activity log entry includes comprehensive audit information: the timestamp when the action occurred, the member account attribution, the type of action performed, the entity type and ID that was affected, and optional details containing old/new values or reasons for the action. This information supports compliance requirements, forensic analysis, and organizational transparency.

Related operations include PATCH /activity-logs for paginated list retrieval with filtering capabilities, and GET /members/{memberId} for retrieving information about the member who performed the logged action.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query the hrm_platform_activity_logs table by primary key ID. Validate that the requesting member has org:manage permission in the current organization context. Enforce organization isolation by verifying the activity log's organization_id matches the member's current organization. Join with hrm_platform_members table to include member information if needed for response enrichment. Return the complete activity log entity including all fields: id, member_id, organization_id, action_type, target_entity_type, target_entity_id, details, created_at, updated_at. Handle not-found scenarios when the activity log ID doesn't exist or belongs to a different organization. Ensure soft-deleted records (deleted_at is not null) are excluded from results unless explicitly querying for deleted entries.

responseBody.description: Complete activity log entry with full audit details

parameters.description: Target activity log entry's unique identifier (UUID)
parameters.name: activityLogId

operations.description:
Invite a new employee to the organization by sending an invitation to an email address.

This operation allows users with employee:manage permission to invite new employees to join the organization. When an invitation is sent, the system checks if the email address already has a user account in the platform. If the email has an existing account, the user is immediately added to the organization as an employee with the specified role. If the email has no existing account, a pending invitation is created that remains active until the user signs up with that email address.

The inviting user must have the employee:manage permission in the current organization context. The system validates this permission before processing the invitation. If the email address already has a pending invitation to the organization, the request is rejected to prevent duplicate invitations.

This endpoint is part of the employee onboarding workflow and is typically used during organization setup or when expanding the team. After successful invitation, the invited user receives a notification with sign-up instructions if they don't have an account yet.
operations.name: invite
operations.specification:
1. Validate that the requesting user has employee:manage permission in the current organization context.
2. Check if the provided email address already has a pending invitation to this organization - reject if duplicate exists.
3. Query hrm_platform_members table to check if email already has an account.
4. If member exists: Create hrm_platform_employees record linking the member to the organization with the specified role, department (optional), position, and employment type.
5. If member doesn't exist: Create pending invitation record (implementation depends on invitation storage pattern).
6. Log the invitation action to hrm_platform_activity_logs with action type 'employee_invited'.
7. Return the created employee record or invitation confirmation.
8. Handle edge cases: email already a member (return existing employee), invalid role ID (reject), organization context missing (reject).

responseBody.description: Created employee record or invitation confirmation

requestBody.description: Employee invitation details including email and role assignment

operations.description:
Retrieve project dashboard statistics and overview information for the organization.

This endpoint provides aggregated project metrics for the organization dashboard, including project counts by status (active, archived, completed), budget utilization statistics, and highlights of projects consuming significant budget percentage. Users with report:view permission can access this data to monitor organizational project health and resource allocation.

The response includes summary statistics such as total active projects, projects approaching or exceeding budget thresholds (over 80% utilization), and top projects by hours logged in the current week. This enables managers and owners to quickly assess project performance and identify projects requiring attention.

Access is restricted to members with report:view permission within the organization context. All data is isolated to the authenticated user's current organization session.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Query hrm_platform_projects table filtered by organization_id from session context. Calculate aggregate statistics: count projects by status (active, archived, completed), calculate budget utilization percentage for projects with budget_hours set (actual hours from timelogs / budget_hours * 100), identify projects with budget utilization over 80%. Join with hrm_platform_timelogs to sum actual hours per project for the current week. Return aggregated dashboard data including total project counts, budget utilization metrics, and top projects by hours logged this week. Apply organization data isolation - only return projects belonging to the authenticated user's current organization.

responseBody.description: Project dashboard statistics including counts by status, budget utilization metrics, and top projects

operations.description:
Retrieve budget utilization analytics for a specific project.

This endpoint provides real-time budget tracking information by comparing the project's allocated budget hours against the actual hours logged by employees through timelogs. The response includes the budget hours defined on the project, the sum of all time entries recorded against the project, the consumption percentage, and remaining budget hours.

The actual hours are calculated by aggregating all timelog durations (duration_minutes field) associated with the project, excluding soft-deleted timelogs. The consumption percentage is computed as (actual_hours / budget_hours) * 100. When budget_hours is null (no budget constraint defined), the percentage and remaining hours fields return null.

This operation requires the report:view permission within the organization context. Users with this permission can access budget analytics for any project in their organization. The endpoint is designed for dashboard widgets, budget monitoring reports, and project health visualization components.

Related operations include GET /projects/{projectId} for retrieving complete project details and PATCH /projects for searching and filtering projects by various criteria including budget status.
operations.name: budget
operations.specification: Query the hrm_platform_projects table to retrieve the project's budget_hours value. Aggregate timelog durations from hrm_platform_timelogs table filtered by project_id, summing duration_minutes and converting to hours (divide by 60). Calculate budget consumption percentage as (actual_hours / budget_hours) * 100. Handle null budget_hours case by returning null for percentage. Filter timelogs to exclude soft-deleted records. Return project identifier, budget hours, actual hours, consumption percentage, and remaining hours. Ensure organization context validation - verify the requesting user has access to the project's organization. Check report:view permission before allowing access.

responseBody.description: Project budget utilization analytics with budget hours, actual hours, consumption percentage, and remaining hours

operations.description:
Retrieve aggregated time tracking analytics for a specific project.

This operation provides comprehensive time analytics for the specified project, including total hours logged, breakdown by employee, breakdown by task, billable versus non-billable time distribution, and time distribution across date ranges. The analytics are computed from the hrm_platform_timelogs table filtered by the project_id.

Access requires the member actor to have the report:view permission within the organization that owns the project. The endpoint validates that the requesting user belongs to the organization and has appropriate role permissions before returning analytics data.

The request body supports filtering by date range to analyze time entries within specific periods, employee filtering to focus on specific team members, task filtering to analyze time spent on specific work items, and billable status filtering to separate billable from non-billable hours. Grouping options allow the response to be organized by employee, by task, by date, or by week for different analytical perspectives.

Related operations include PATCH /timelogs for detailed timelog listings and GET /projects/{projectId} for project metadata. The analytics data is read-only and computed on-demand from current timelog records.
operations.name: analyticsTime
operations.specification: Query hrm_platform_timelogs table filtered by project_id path parameter. Apply request body filters: date range (date >= fromDate AND date <= toDate), employee_id IN (employeeIds), task_id IN (taskIds), billable equality. Compute aggregations: SUM(duration_minutes) for total hours, GROUP BY employee_id for employee breakdown, GROUP BY task_id for task breakdown, GROUP BY DATE(date) for daily breakdown, GROUP BY billable for billable split. Join with hrm_platform_employees for employee names if grouping by employee. Join with hrm_platform_tasks for task names if grouping by task. Validate user has report:view permission in project's organization. Return aggregated statistics with pagination not required as this is analytics summary data. Handle edge case: project with no timelogs returns zero totals with empty breakdowns.

responseBody.description: Aggregated time analytics for the project

requestBody.description: Analytics query filters and grouping options

operations.description:
Retrieve all projects assigned to the current authenticated employee through their project memberships.

This operation provides employees with visibility into their project commitments by querying the hrm_platform_project_members table for all active memberships associated with the authenticated employee. For each membership record, the endpoint returns combined information including project details (name, color_code, status) and the employee's role within that project (member or project-lead).

Only non-deleted project membership records are returned (deleted_at IS NULL on hrm_platform_project_members). Projects are returned regardless of their lifecycle status (active, archived, or completed) to provide complete historical context of the employee's project involvement. The response includes the employee's role designation for each project, which determines their task management permissions - project-leads can create and manage tasks while regular members cannot.

Authentication is required as a member actor. The employee context is automatically derived from the current session token, ensuring strict data isolation where each employee can only view their own project assignments. This endpoint is essential for employees to understand their responsibilities and access levels across different projects within the organization.

Related operations: GET /hrmPlatform/projects/{projectId} for detailed project information, POST /hrmPlatform/projects/{projectId}/tasks for project-leads to create tasks.
operations.name: list
operations.specification: Query hrm_platform_project_members table filtering by current employee's ID and deleted_at IS NULL. Join with hrm_platform_projects table to fetch project details. Return array of project summaries with membership role information. Order by project created_at descending or by project name ascending. No pagination needed as employees typically have limited project assignments. Include project fields: id, name, color_code, status, and membership role. Exclude projects from deleted memberships.

responseBody.description: Array of project membership summaries including project details and employee's role

operations.description:
Stop a running timer and automatically create a timelog entry.

This endpoint allows employees to stop their active timer session, which triggers automatic timelog creation. The system calculates the work duration by measuring the elapsed time between the timer's start timestamp and the current stop time, then rounds the duration to the nearest minute.

The created timelog inherits all tracking context from the timer including the project, optional task, and work description. The billable flag on the timelog defaults to true. After successful execution, the timer's stopped_at field is populated and the timer is no longer considered active.

This operation enforces that the timer must exist, must belong to the requesting employee, and must currently be running (stopped_at is null). If the timer was already stopped or does not exist, the request is rejected with an appropriate error response.

The single active timer constraint means employees must stop or discard their current timer before starting a new one. This stop operation is the primary pathway for converting live time tracking into permanent timelog records.
operations.name: stop
operations.specification:
Query the hrm_platform_timers table by timerId and verify the timer exists and belongs to the authenticated employee. Check that stopped_at is null to confirm the timer is still running. If any validation fails, return 404 or 400 error.

Calculate the duration by computing the difference between current timestamp and started_at, then round to nearest minute (durations under 30 seconds round to 0). Begin a database transaction to ensure atomicity.

Create a new record in hrm_platform_timelogs table with: employee_id from timer, project_id from timer, task_id from timer (if present), date extracted from started_at, duration_minutes as calculated, description from timer, billable set to true.

Update the timer record by setting stopped_at to current timestamp. Commit the transaction.

Return the created timelog object. Log the action to hrm_platform_activity_logs with action type 'timelog_created' and reference to both timer and timelog IDs.

responseBody.description: The created timelog entry from stopping the timer

operations.description:
Reject a submitted timesheet with a required rejection reason.

This operation allows users with time approval permissions to reject timesheets that have been submitted for review. The rejection reason is mandatory and must provide clear feedback to the employee about what needs to be corrected. When a timesheet is rejected, the system records the review timestamp, the identity of the reviewer, and the detailed rejection reason.

The timesheet status transitions from submitted to rejected, and then automatically returns to draft status, allowing the employee to address the issues and resubmit. All timelogs included in the timesheet remain unlocked and editable after rejection.

This operation validates that the timesheet is in submitted status before allowing rejection. Attempts to reject timesheets in draft, approved, or already rejected status will be rejected. The requesting user must have the time:approve permission within the organization context.
operations.name: reject
operations.specification: Validate the requesting member has time:approve permission within the organization context. Query the timesheet by ID and verify it exists and is not soft deleted. Validate the timesheet status is 'submitted' - reject if draft, approved, or already rejected. Validate the rejection_reason is provided and not empty (minimum 1 character). Update the timesheet: set status to 'rejected', set reviewed_at to current timestamp, set reviewed_by_id to the requesting member's ID, set rejection_reason to the provided value. The timesheet automatically returns to draft status after rejection, allowing the employee to modify and resubmit. Record an activity log entry for the rejection action. Return the updated timesheet with the new status and rejection details.

responseBody.description: Updated timesheet with rejected status and rejection details

requestBody.description: Rejection details including the mandatory rejection reason

prerequisites.description: Timesheet must be created before it can be rejected. The timesheet creation establishes the employee ownership and weekly period, and the timesheet must later be submitted to reach the 'submitted' status required for rejection.

Used when a member's access token has expired and they need to obtain new tokens without re-authenticating. The refresh_token field contains the valid refresh token that was issued during login or a previous refresh operation.
